# Dense Lean module directories

This audit counts direct production `.lean` modules, excluding `.lake`,
vendored sources, scripts, and test modules. A large directory is split when
several files form one proof chain or share a
specific mathematical subject. Independently reusable concepts remain in the
owning directory. For Lemma 3.5, `DriftedTube/FiniteVarianceLower/EndpointBounds.lean`
is the entry point and `DriftedTube/FiniteVarianceLower/Lemmas/Staircase/`
contains its one-purpose proof chain. Reusable real-width endpoint estimates,
block events, and moving-tube inclusions remain in `HorizontalTube/` and at
the `DriftedTube/` subject level. `Lemmas/` marks the module role; only Lean's
`private` modifier restricts a declaration to its defining module. A move
preserves theorem statements and proofs. An API rename updates every client
and removes the old declaration; do not keep a forwarding or deprecated
compatibility alias. A move changes import paths. A directory grouping alone
does not require a namespace rename; change the namespace when mathematical
ownership changes, and record deliberate namespace retention when the move
only clarifies module organization.

Date-stamped notes below are historical checkpoints. The latest inventory
and remaining-work statement is in the final section of this file.

## Reorganized proof families

| Family | Main entry or subject | Internal organization |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Probability/Kernel/Step` | Measurable transition kernels induced by noisy and killed steps | `Basic.lean` constructs total and option-valued steps; `Path.lean` defines finite histories and their measurability; `Iteration.lean` treats arbitrary noise measures and survival; and `Endpoint.lean` adds a terminal target. The finite weighted branch constructor, its survival weights, and its canonical-IID comparison are grouped in `FiniteBranches/{Basic,Survival,IID}.lean`. All seven modules expose complete interfaces; no proof-only `Lemmas/` collection is needed. The finite branch index is the only finiteness assumption in `FiniteBranches/Basic.lean`; its state space may be countable and its target need not be finite. |
| `Probability/Kernel/FiniteState` | Kernel representations on a genuinely finite state space | `Matrix.lean` converts nonnegative substochastic matrices to kernels and relates matrix multiplication to kernel composition. The generic row-substochastic matrix condition belongs to `LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Substochastic.lean`; the finite weighted branch constructor belongs to `Kernel/Step/FiniteBranches/Basic.lean` and permits a general measurable target. |
| `RandomWalk/SmallDeviation/DriftedTube` | `FiniteVarianceLower/EndpointBounds.lean` contains both endpoint conclusions of Wang Yiyang, *Asymptotic Speed of the N-Branching Random Walk with Infinite Offspring*, Chapter 3, Lemma 3.5; `FiniteVarianceUpper/Basic.lean` formalizes Chapter 3, Lemma 3.4 | `Event.lean` owns the full tilted-tube event; `BlockEvent.lean` owns the reusable pair and full-sequence events for one finite block. `FiniteVarianceUpper/Lemmas/Blocks.lean` contains the theorem-specific conditional block proof. The bin endpoints, narrowed width, and terminal fractions are internal parameters in `FiniteVarianceLower/Lemmas/Staircase/Setup/Binning.lean`; the ordinary and terminal block windows and horizontal sub-tube geometry are grouped in `Setup/EndpointWindow.lean` and `Setup/BlockTube.lean`. The finite-cover proof and parameter selection are in `FiniteVarianceLower/Lemmas/Staircase/Binning/`. `HorizontalTube/EndpointWindow/RealWidthLower.lean` owns reusable real-width endpoint-window bounds; `HorizontalTube/Blocks/` owns generic block events, conditional bounds, and product estimates. `BlockInclusion.lean` owns the reusable moving-tube inclusion. `FiniteVarianceLower/Lemmas/Staircase/` contains the Lemma 3.5 proof assembly, divided into `Setup`, `Endpoint`, `Rate`, `Concrete`, and block steps. `EndpointWindow/Basic.lean` defines the lower endpoint-window event, and `EndpointWindow/Reflection.lean` proves its reflected upper-window correspondence. These statements require no finite-variance assumptions, so they are grouped at the `DriftedTube` subject level; `FiniteVarianceLower/EndpointBounds.lean` consumes them in Lemma 3.5. The generic quotient/remainder schedule and its natural-number count, endpoint, and block-length facts are in `Combinatorics/Sequence/TailMergedBlock.lean`; the balanced finite list is constructed by `Combinatorics/Sequence/BalancedPartition.lean`, and `Analysis/Asymptotics/Scale/Block/Partition.lean` contains its asymptotic limits. The Lemma 3.5-specific tube-width and endpoint margins stay under `FiniteVarianceLower/Lemmas/Staircase/Setup/`, while the block exponential product and the entrance-rate allocation are grouped in `FiniteVarianceLower/Lemmas/Staircase/Rate/BlockExponential.lean`. `FiniteVarianceLower/Lemmas/Staircase/Concrete/` contains the theorem-specific lower and upper bound assembly. |
| `RandomWalk/SmallDeviation/Drawdown` | `FiniteVarianceUpper/Theorems.lean` formalizes Wang Yiyang, *Asymptotic Speed of the N-Branching Random Walk with Infinite Offspring*, Chapter 3, Lemma 3.3 and its uniform consequence | `Path/Event/Drawdown.lean` owns the reusable finite-history drawdown predicates and their measurability. The finite-prefix path, spatial-bin definitions, jump-pattern events, factors, and admissible pattern family are specific to Lemma 3.3 and live under `FiniteVarianceUpper/Lemmas/JumpPattern/`; the running maximum uses Mathlib's general `partialSups` API directly. `FiniteVarianceUpper/Lemmas/TubeEvent.lean` defines the finite-pair and sequence-level block tube events used only by this proof's conditional-block and jump-pattern steps. `FiniteVarianceUpper/Lemmas/ConditionalBlocks.lean`, `Lemmas/JumpPattern/`, and `Lemmas/Rate/` contain the non-reusable conditional tube, rounded-maximum jump, union-bound, and rate proofs. General conditional event iteration was moved to `Probability/Process/Filtration/ConditionalBlocks.lean`; translation of finite interval events moved beside its definition in `Path/Window/Basic.lean`, and IID finite-block interval-law transfer moved to `Path/Block/Law/FiniteInterval.lean`. The generic quotient estimate for a horizon divided by a floor-rounded block length is in `Analysis/Asymptotics/Scale/Block/Length.lean`. DriftedTube now uses `Fin.partialSum` and finite sums directly instead of importing Drawdown's finite-sum aliases. `Scaling.lean` remains outside the proof tree because its scaling identities apply to general event sets. |
| `RandomWalk/SmallDeviation/Range` | Independent bounded-range and block-oscillation small-deviation estimates | The five subject-level modules have separate interfaces: `BlockDonsker.lean` transfers finite-block oscillation probabilities to Brownian range events; `FiniteCoverUpper.lean` gives the fixed-cover block estimate; `QuadraticEnergyCover.lean` constructs the exponent-two finite corridor cover; `BlockOscillation.lean` gives the finite-variance exponential block bound; and `Rate.lean` assembles the finite-variance range rate. The general finite-horizon IID range-to-block inequality lives at `RandomWalk/Path/Block/Partition/Range.lean`, since it assumes no small-deviation or moment hypotheses. The three deterministic block-to-path inclusions used by the last two rate proofs are in the non-reusable `Lemmas/BlockCorridor.lean`, imported with `import all`. Mathlib provides the general extended diameter API through `Metric.ediam`, so no duplicate general metric oscillation theorem is introduced here ([Mathlib diameter API](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Topology/EMetricSpace/Diam.html)). The generic index-type range cover is in `Order/Bounds/RangeCover.lean`, with its path-space adapter in `Topology/Cadlag/Skorokhod/SmallDeviation/RangeCover.lean`. These estimates are separate from the Lemma 3.3 drawdown proof, which uses Lemma 3.2 directly. |

Under `SparreAndersen/Rotation/`, `Cover.lean` owns the finite path event cover, `Basic.lean` owns the cyclic survival event and its preimage and measurability interfaces, `FiniteProduct.lean` owns IID finite-product invariance and the finite endpoint-to-survival probability inequality, and `Probability.lean` transfers the inequality to the canonical infinite IID sequence law. `Composition/{InclusionExclusion,CyclicGapSum,EndpointProbability}.lean` expose the finite-measure inclusion--exclusion identity and the iid endpoint expansions. The probability-independent cyclic-gap construction and positive-composition reindexing now live under `Combinatorics/Sequence/CyclicGap/{Basic,Reindex}.lean` in `Combinatorics.Sequence`; `CyclicGap/Lemmas/Composition.lean` contains only the inverse proof chain. `Composition/Lemmas/BlockProbability/{Event,Measure,IIDFactorization}.lean` keeps the proof-specific adjacent-block event, measure identity, and iid gap factorization. The result has no N-selection or branching-walk hypotheses, so it is owned here rather than under a particular speed application. |
| `Probability/Process/Path`, `Probability/Process/TimeGrid`, and `Probability/Process/Brownian/AboveStart` | General path events, deterministic process-time grids, and their Brownian specializations | `TimeGrid/Ceiling.lean` gives the generic ceiling of an arbitrary extended nonnegative time functional by a finite monotone grid, with order, convergence, and measurability results; its selector uses Mathlib's `MeasureTheory.hittingBtwn`. `TimeGrid/UnitInterval.lean` and `TimeGrid/Expanding.lean` provide deterministic grids. The reusable density of the canonical inclusion $\mathbb Q_{\ge 0}\hookrightarrow\mathbb R_{\ge 0}$ is owned by `Topology/Order/NNReal/Rational.lean`, independent of process-time grids. `Path/FirstPassage/GridApproximation.lean` specializes the generic ceiling interface to continuous-path first passage and owns path-locality and reflection-continuity results. Brownian reflection at the selected time is in `Brownian/Reflection/FirstPassage/GridLaw.lean`; finite path observations use `hittingBtwn` directly in `Grid.lean`. `Path/FirstPassage/` also groups descending-hitting-time, reflection, and restart interfaces. `Path/AboveStart/FirstWindow/` owns the generic continuous-path time, running-minimum characterization, and uncentered/centered shift maps. `Brownian/AboveStart/FirstWindow/` contains Brownian-law specializations; its `Lemmas/` directory holds the finite-window boundary, existence, interior-return, and endpoint-return proof stages, while `Shift/` owns their Brownian continuity and cutoff-limit consequences. The namespaces and module paths therefore separate general path constructions from process-specific laws. Random-walk path foundations are grouped into `Path/Adapted/` (filtration and martingale), `Path/Event/` (drawdown, survival, oscillation, and last sign change), and `Path/Representation/` (càdlàg paths, interpolation, and scaling); the `Basic`, `Window`, and `Skorokhod` entry modules remain at the root. |

These statements are independent of probability processes and provide the countable dense evaluation coordinates used by continuous-path laws. |
| `Topology/Cadlag/Skorokhod` | Reusable topology and geometry for càdlàg paths with the Skorokhod metric | Public interfaces are grouped under `Compactness/`, `Corridor/`, `EDistance/`, `Evaluation/`, `Maps/`, `Oscillation/`, `Path/`, and `TimeChange/`. Under `Evaluation/`, `Basic.lean` states continuity at continuity times, `Integral.lean` owns continuity of bounded-continuous integral functionals, `Measurable.lean` owns fixed-time Borel evaluation, and `Joint.lean` owns variable-time Borel evaluation. The fixed-time and joint measurability results now cover arbitrary metric Borel state spaces. `Maps/Continuous.lean` owns the continuous embedding from continuous paths into Skorokhod space; its measurability follows from continuity without a second-countability assumption on the state space. `Topology.lean` remains the subject-level topology interface. `TimeChange/FinitePartition/` owns the piecewise-affine clock matching finite partitions and the resulting step-path and logarithmic-distortion bounds; the one-use secant-slope estimate and its proof chain are grouped under `FinitePartition/Lemmas/`. `TimeChange/Limit/` groups the summable-distortion convergence chain; `EDistance/Logarithmic/Completion/` groups the aligned Cauchy construction, subsequence extraction, limit identification, and completeness theorem. These are complete reusable convergence results, so they are grouped by mathematical role rather than under `Lemmas/`. |
| `BranchingProcessTest` | Tests for the production library | Test modules are grouped by topic. Mogul'skii tests use `Mogulskii/{Axiom,Path,PathClass,Rates,Regression}/`; stable tests use `Attraction/`, `PathLaw/`, `RandomWalk/`, and `SmallDeviation/`; restart tests use `Branching/Restart/Trial/` and `Branching/Restart/Lineage/`; Skorokhod tests are grouped by topology operation. `scripts/run-all-lean-tests.py` and CI log paths follow these locations. |
| `Combinatorics/BranchingWalk/Basic` | Shared data and basic branching-walk operations | `Genealogy/` contains ancestor, descendant, and generation-size results; `Position/` contains displacement and position maps; `Sibling/` contains parent/sibling relations and closure properties; `Survival/` contains realized-particle and path-survival predicates; `Ordering/` contains orderability. `Definitions.lean` and `Map.lean` remain directly under `Basic/` as shared foundations. |
| `Combinatorics/BranchingWalk/Step/Selection` | Deterministic operations on finite selections of offspring slots | `Finite.lean` defines finite selections of surviving slots; `Potential.lean` and `Slot.lean` give deterministic reserve and slot-order interfaces; `FiniteSlot.lean` encodes a capacity-two selection as a binary offspring step. |
| `Combinatorics/BranchingWalk/Genealogy` | Infinite lineages and permanent survival of rooted branching walks | `Survival.lean` defines finite-depth survival, arbitrary-depth descendants, and an infinite surviving lineage; under finite children at every surviving prefix of the specified root it proves `HasArbitrarilyDeepDescendant root ↔ HasInfiniteLineage root`. The proof directly uses Mathlib’s `exists_seq_forall_proj_of_forall_finite` inverse-system form of Kőnig’s infinity lemma (pinned revision `380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51`). This is a complete subject interface, separate from the finite ancestor/descendant and generation-size operations in `Basic/Genealogy/`; its local proof is contained in the result, so a `Lemmas/` subtree is not needed. |
| `Combinatorics/BranchingWalk/Population/Candidates` | Deterministic root-indexed candidates and admissibility for a generation | `Generation.lean` defines the surviving child-address set of a finite parent population and connects it to the generic offspring-address set. `ExponentialWeight.lean` proves that finite negative exponential offspring weight makes its real-position lower sections finite, without a probability law or measurable-space assumption. The field-observable specialization and domain-flow measurability result belong in `Probability/BranchingRandomWalk/Population/Candidates/RootIndexed/`. |
| `Probability/BranchingRandomWalk/Population/Candidates` | Candidate populations in a root-indexed branching-random-walk field | `Prefix.lean` and `MultiRoot.lean` define finite child candidates; `Ordering.lean` and `Leftmost.lean` rank them by particle position and address; `FullChildren.lean` and `FullSelection.lean` compare finite slot truncations with the full offspring set. `RootIndexed/RealPosition.lean` connects the deterministic real-position lower-finiteness theorem to the generation-truncated field observable, while `RootIndexed/Measurability.lean` and `Adapted.lean` prove fixed-parent and adapted candidate measurability. The one-use finite-prefix comparison chain is in `Lemmas/FullSelection.lean`. |
| `Combinatorics/Selection/NSelection` | Generic deterministic capacity-`N` selection | `Basic.lean` defines selectors on arbitrary candidate sets; `Mechanism/` gives ordered first-`N` rules, value ranking, and order transport; `Matching/` gives generic Hall and equal-rank criteria. These definitions use sets, finite sets, and order and carry no measurable-space, branching-genealogy, offspring, or generation data. |
| ``Combinatorics/BranchingWalk/Selection/`NSelection` | Capacity-`N` selection applied to deterministic branching walks | `Walk/` defines the generation recursion from offspring sets and the resulting cloud, frontier, and speed; `Coupling/` proves cloud, offspring, and pathwise comparisons. The generic selector is imported from `Combinatorics/Selection/NSelection`; this subtree is where it acquires branching-walk semantics. |
| `MeasureTheory/Selection` | Measurable environment-dependent and domain-flow-adapted selection | `Random.lean` defines general set-valued and capacity-$N$ mechanisms; `Finite/{Basic,Causal,ByValue}.lean` gives finite-input, domain-flow, and measurable value-ranked forms; `NSelection/` proves measurability of generic ranked capacity-$N$ selectors; `Causal.lean` handles arbitrary candidate sets; `Process.lean` forms measurable selected populations. These types use measurable candidate spaces and information domains without branching data. Root-indexed and cloud-coupling applications remain under `Probability/BranchingRandomWalk/Selection/`; the generic causal finite-selection overflow stopping time belongs under `Probability/Process/Stopping/Selection/Overflow.lean`. |
| `MeasureTheory/BranchingWalk/Step/Selection` | Measurability of operations on finite offspring selections | `FirstN.lean`, `Potential.lean`, and `Slot.lean` give measurable versions of the corresponding deterministic step-selection operations; `FiniteSlot.lean` proves measurability of the binary-slot offspring encoding. |
| `Probability/BranchingRandomWalk/Spine` | Spine random walks, many-to-one identities, and tube moments | `ManyToOne/`, `RandomWalk/`, `PointMeasure/`, and `Tilted/` group the corresponding public constructions. `Path/` groups lineage-generation observables, many-to-one identities, and second-moment results by subject; `Path/SecondMoment/Basic.lean` owns pathwise diagonal/off-diagonal and MRCA decompositions, while `Path/SecondMoment/SubtreeLaws.lean` owns distinct-child subtree laws and integrated second-moment identities. The IID finite-history integral recursions belong to the general random-walk path interface at `Probability/Process/RandomWalk/Path/Measure.lean`; Spine modules import them for their proof chains. `Tube/` groups corridor and tube-specific second-moment estimates; within `Tube/MRCA/`, `Expansion.lean` handles path-level corridor splitting, `Prefix.lean` factors weighted ancestral-prefix observables, and `PositiveDepth.lean` defines and bounds the affine-tube contribution at every MRCA depth, including the root split at depth zero. `MRCA/Lemmas/ChildPairBound.lean` contains the technical shifted-corridor stages for the root-split term. `ActualContribution.lean` connects the path-level decomposition to the depth-indexed contribution. The declaration namespaces remain rooted at `ProbabilityTheory.BranchingRandomWalk.Spine`. |

The deterministic encoding itself is owned by `Combinatorics/BranchingWalk/Step/Selection/FiniteSlot.lean`, and its measurability by `MeasureTheory/BranchingWalk/Step/Selection/FiniteSlot.lean`. |

| `Probability/Process/Stable/PathLaw` | Càdlàg path laws for stable clock processes and stable Lévy processes | `Basic.lean` states the general stable-clock path-law interface; `UnitInterval.lean` constructs its canonical finite-horizon law. `Concatenation.lean` builds a full-time process from i.i.d. unit blocks, and `FullProcess.lean` proves independent increments and stable increment laws. `MonotoneGrid.lean` extends strict finite-grid laws to grids with repeated times; `LinearTube.lean` proves positive mass of Gaussian stable path balls around linear paths. These are complete reusable path-law constructions and theorems; their module-local grid and bridge computations remain private. |

The comparison and positivity calculations remain private within their theorem modules. |
| `Probability/Process/Stable/SmallDeviation` | Stable-process small-deviation event interfaces and probability comparisons | The subject root owns the rational range tube, block endpoint-bin lower bound, corridor/range logarithmic comparison, shifted-corridor entrance comparison, and endpoint-constrained comparison. `Blocks/` owns stable time-space rescaling and adjacent-block entrance factorization; these complete stable-process event interfaces are distinct from the theorem-specific construction modules under `Blocks/Lower/` and `Blocks/Upper/`. `EscapeRate/` owns the process-level limits and finite-horizon path-law transfer. |
| `Probability/Process/Path/Skorokhod/Corridor/UniformBlocks` | Finite uniform partitions of path corridors | `Basic.lean` owns the uniform rational block clock, translated block paths, tube events, and their structural/measurability facts; `Prefix.lean` owns stopped prefix paths and their block increments; `Events.lean` owns the corresponding measurable block and prefix events. `Gluing.lean` defines path-space corridors and proves endpoint-bin concatenation; `Cover.lean` groups rational-time block coverage with the resulting whole-path corridor and tube comparisons. `Probability/{Bounds,Independence,Stationarity}.lean` state general product bounds, block-path independence, and equality in law under independent stationary increments. Stable lower-bound clients apply the generic `IsOrderedMonoid.pow_le_of_mul_le_succ` recurrence directly to these prefix-event probabilities; no event-specific wrapper is kept. `Feedback/{Basic,FullPath,Probability}.lean` define adaptive endpoint-selected events, transfer rational bounds to càdlàg paths, and prove the corresponding probability lower bounds. |
| `Probability/Process/RandomWalk/FunctionalLimit/Stable` | Stable-domain path-law convergence and tightness | `PathLaw/` groups endpoint-grid identification, subsequential law construction, process-law construction, and convergence. `Tightness/` groups block tails, local oscillation, partition bounds, compact-range control, and the resulting tightness theorem. | `Probability/Process/Brownian/SmallDeviation/Range` | Brownian range small-width probability bounds and their exponential rate | `EscapeConstant.lean` gives the standard Brownian path-law escape coefficient; `FiniteCover.lean` gives the fixed finite-corridor spectral estimate; `UpperRate.lean` derives the small-width logarithmic upper rate. In `Bounds/`, `{Lower,Upper,SharpUpper,StrictInterior}.lean` contains complete rate-transfer and tube-bound results; the finite-cover block estimate, parameter choice, and logarithmic transfer used only for `SharpUpper` remain under `Bounds/Lemmas/SharpUpper/`. Mathlib `BinaryTree` is a fixed binary-node datatype, while `UlamHarris.Tree` is an arbitrary-slot, prefix-closed set of finite addresses; Mathlib has no matching replacement ([pinned Mathlib source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51/Mathlib/Data/Tree/Basic.lean)). |

Ordering properties, ranks, and ordering induced by potentials are under `Ordering/`; slot selection and sibling closure are under `Selection/`; point-measure operations are under `Measure/`; generation-local updates are under `Generation/`. |

Root-indexed position measurability remains under `Position/`. |

## Abstraction review: stationary increment path laws (2026-10-19)

This review was triggered by repeated use of translated block-path laws. The
checked Mathlib revision is
`380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51`. The official
[independent-increment API](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Probability/Independence/Process/HasIndepIncrements/Basic.html)
defines independence of increments along every finite monotone time grid.
The official
[finite-dimensional-law API](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Probability/Process/FiniteDimensionalLaws.html)
characterizes equality of process laws by equality of all finite-dimensional
distributions. These are the general ingredients used here; neither API
packages equal-duration time changes of a process with stationary independent
increments. The local
`Probability.Process.IndepIncrements.FiniteDimensional` API already proves
function-valued law equality from matching increment laws and zero starts, and
`Probability.Process.IndepIncrements.FiniteObservations.DisjointPaths` already gives independence
for arbitrary observed path coordinates on adjacent intervals and for finite
monotone partitions. The literature uses stationary independent increments as
the defining increment structure of a Lévy process; see the
[Cambridge excerpt of Sato, *Lévy Processes and Infinitely Divisible
Distributions*](https://assets.cambridge.org/97811076/56499/excerpt/9781107656499_excerpt.pdf).

The resulting public path-law theorem is
`HasIndepIncrements.process_identDistrib_of_sameDuration_timeChanges` in
`Probability/Process/IndepIncrements/PathLaw/StationaryTimeChange.lean`. It
assumes independent increments, stationary increments, monotone maps
`τ, τ' : I → T`, and
`τ t - τ s = τ' t - τ' s` whenever `s ≤ t`; it concludes equality in law of
the centered paths
`q ↦ X (τ q) - X (τ ⊥)` and
`q ↦ X (τ' q) - X (τ' ⊥)`, with almost-everywhere measurability of those path
maps. Its time type is an ordered additive commutative monoid with ordered
subtraction, its index is any linearly ordered type with a least element, and
its state is a measurable additive commutative group. The proof reduces path
increments to equal-duration one-increment laws and then applies the local
finite-dimensional uniqueness theorem. It needs no zero-start, càdlàg, stable,
moment, or scaling assumption. This is the most abstract useful form found:
it adds the equal-duration path-law operation absent from Mathlib while
retaining the standard hypotheses that make its proof work.

The complete-segment corridor consequences live beside their event semantics
in `Probability/Process/Path/Skorokhod/Corridor/SegmentStationarity.lean`.
They additionally require almost-surely càdlàg paths to pass from rational
coordinates to all times, but do not require a Lévy or stable-process record.
For finite rational uniform partitions, the named block-path interface in
`UniformBlocks/Probability/Independence.lean` specializes the more general
`DisjointPaths` results. The two retained statements expose canonical
partition paths used by the corridor factorization and upper-block arguments;
the unused adjacent-block specialization was removed because
`indepFun_adjacentPaths` already states the more general result. The
stable-only block-law wrapper under `Stable/SmallDeviation/Blocks/Lemmas/`
was also removed: its callers now use the general rational-block law directly,
supplying only the independent- and stationary-increment properties inherited
from the stable process. The stable-only prefix/next-block independence alias
was removed for the same reason; its callers invoke the general
`UniformBlocks/Probability/Independence` theorem. The entrance/continuation independence
calculation remains private in `EntranceFactorization.lean` because only that
file's event-factorization proofs use it.

The same review compared the arbitrary-horizon return-corridor scaling laws in
`Blocks/ReturnScale.lean` with their first-uniform-block specializations. The
arbitrary-horizon centered-path and corridor identities remain at the Stable
small-deviation block level as complete scaling results. The first-block
return identity is used only by lower block-bound proofs, so it now lives in
`Blocks/ReturnScale.lean`; it is derived from the arbitrary-horizon identity
and the canonical first-block path equation. The unused first-block
specialization for the left-open endpoint convention, the unused forward
orientation, and a positivity corollary that only rewrote an existing scaling
identity were removed. The proof-only `ReturnScale` dependency of
`EntranceScaling.lean` is now an ordinary import; its public imports name the
Stable process and path-event interfaces appearing in its theorem statements.

## Same-stem files and directories

Mathlib permits a substantive `Foo.lean` interface beside `Foo/` when the
directory holds related component modules; the pinned Mathlib source has 112
such pairs, including `Tactic/Linarith.lean` beside `Tactic/Linarith/`. This
repository currently has no same-level `.lean` file and directory with the
same stem in its production or test source trees. The initial inventory found
pairs whose file was only an import facade or whose declarations fit more
clearly in `Foo/Basic.lean`, `Foo/Core.lean`, or subject-specific children;
those were moved and callers import the owning modules directly. A substantive
entry file remains appropriate when it presents a real interface and the
directory groups its related components. Four import-only facades were
removed:
`NSelection/Coupling.lean`, `Processes/Concurrent.lean`,
`Processes/StepSelection.lean`, and `StepSelection/SplitSchedule.lean`.
Child filenames in the new `Spine/PointMeasure/`, `Spine/Tilted/`, and
branching-walk families use short subject-relative names instead of repeating
their parent directory. A repository-wide follow-up scan also normalized
`Analysis/Asymptotics/Power/PowerTailIntegral.lean` and

`SumLower.lean`; `Probability/BranchingRandomWalk/Genealogy/Lineage/Lineages.lean`

are unchanged, and callers import the new paths directly.

## Independent-pair conditional section abstraction review (2026-10-21)

The former `Probability/Sequence/IID/Blocks/Conditional.lean` stated a
conditional-expectation identity for consecutive blocks of an IID sequence,
then derived upper and lower bounds for event sections. Its three clients
were the drawdown, drifted-tube, and horizontal-tube block estimates. That
reuse prompted a search for the actual abstraction, rather than an outward
move based only on the number of callers.

At the pinned Mathlib revision
`380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51`,
`Mathlib/Probability/Kernel/CondDistrib.lean` provides
`condExp_prod_ae_eq_integral_condDistrib` and
`condDistrib_ae_eq_condExp`. The former identifies conditional expectation
with integration against the regular conditional distribution; the latter
identifies that kernel's section probabilities with conditional expectations.
The conditional-distribution API requires a standard Borel future value
space. The project module `Probability/Independence/ConditionalIntegral.lean`
already derives the independent-pair identity
\[
  \mathbb E[f(X,Y)\mid X](\omega)
  =\int f(X(\omega),y)\,d(P\circ Y^{-1})(y)
  \quad\text{for }X\perp Y.
\]
The matching event identity is now stated there as
`IndepFun.condExp_indicator_pairEvent_ae_eq_sectionProbability`:
\[
  \mathbb E[\mathbf 1_E(X,Y)\mid X](\omega)
  =(P\circ Y^{-1})\{y:(X(\omega),y)\in E\}.
\]
It accepts an arbitrary independent pair and a measurable event in the
product of its value spaces, retaining only the standard Borel assumption
required by the current conditional-distribution proof. Mathlib supplies the
underlying integral and kernel identities, but not this event-section
specialization.

This identity is the reusable mathematical operation; the former IID
prefix/next-block equality is its specialization, and the upper/lower section
estimates are direct order consequences. The IID-only file and these thin
wrappers were removed. The three block proofs now use the general identity
with `indepFun_blockCoordinates_blockCoordinates`, keeping their event bounds
local to the model-specific estimates. This places the reusable result in the
independence layer and the sequence-specific fact in
`Probability/Sequence/IID/Blocks/StoppingTime.lean`.

The source comparison used the pinned
[`CondDistrib.lean`](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51/Mathlib/Probability/Kernel/CondDistrib.lean)
and Mathlib's [official API documentation](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Probability/Kernel/CondDistrib.html).
The library-location decision follows the
[Mathlib review guide](https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/pr-review.html#location-location),
which asks reviewers to search for existing general results, select a
semantically appropriate module, and assess whether the addition advances the
library. The generalized theorem, its three block clients, and the
finite-product reindexing clients build locally; the remote preflight's build
step also completed, while its static test step exposed a stale theorem name
in an axiom-check file, corrected in the current working tree.

## Abstraction research: stable constant-corridor rate

A cross-module reuse observation prompted a generality review of
`Probability/Process/Stable/SmallDeviation/PathClass/StepCorridor/ConstantCorridorRate.lean`.
The pinned Mathlib API supplies weak convergence of probability laws and the
continuous mapping theorem in
[`MeasureTheory.Function.ConvergenceInDistribution`](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/ConvergenceInDistribution.html),
but no large-deviation or small-deviation principle for the logarithmic
probability of a shrinking path corridor. The local stable-process layer
already supplies the more general reusable hypotheses and shifted-corridor
rate through `IsStableLevyProcess.exists_shiftedCorridor_escape_rate` and
`HasStableProcessEscapeRate`.

The literature has broader results along different axes: Elena Shmileva,
*Shifted small deviations and Chung LIL for symmetric alpha-stable processes*
(arXiv:0811.2583, 2009), treats arbitrary continuous shifts for symmetric
stable processes with index in `(1, 2)` in the uniform topology; Frank Aurzada
and Steffen Dereich, *Small deviations of general Lévy processes* (Annals of
Probability 37 (2009), 2066–2092, arXiv:0805.1330), treats centered
supremum-norm small deviations for general real-valued Lévy processes. The
first result imposes symmetry and an index range, while the second studies a
centered two-sided supremum corridor. Neither directly subsumes the local
finite, possibly asymmetric constant-corridor statement under the stable path
law assumptions.

The local theorem is therefore kept as a complete constant-corridor
specialization at the path-class rate boundary, built on the stable-process
interfaces above. Its proof-specific scalar rescaling remains local. The
audit removed the duplicate import and the unused public
`scaledPathConstantCorridorEvent` wrapper: the theorem now states its result
using the existing `scaledConstantCorridorEvent`, which is the canonical event
for these bounds. This review records why the result remains a specialization
and does not introduce a second public general-purpose small-deviation API.

## Abstraction research: stationary increments and translated block laws

The uniform-block path-law proof was reviewed against its actual mathematical
hypotheses before promoting its interface. Mathlib's pinned
[`HasIndepIncrements` source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/021c46bdd042f67b538b9f9871d556a93713a9a9/Mathlib/Probability/Independence/Process/HasIndepIncrements/Basic.lean)
defines independent increments for a process over a preorder, but has no
stationary-increment property or translated-process law theorem. Joseph C.
Watkins, *Stochastic Processes in Continuous Time*, Definition 2.1, p. 12,
states stationary increments and independent increments as separate
properties of a process; stationary increments say that the law of
`X_{t+s} - X_t` is independent of `t` ([lecture notes](https://math.arizona.edu/~jwatkins/notesc.pdf)).
The broader time statement below is derived from the ordered additive-time
hypotheses, rather than attributed to Watkins's real-time definition.

The Lean API therefore records stationary increments independently in
`Probability/Process/StationaryIncrements/Basic.lean`, with only an additive
time monoid and subtraction on the state. The finite-dimensional law API in
`Probability/Process/IndepIncrements/FiniteDimensional.lean` takes values in a
measurable additive commutative group with measurable addition. Its
finite-dimensional position-law theorem uses an explicit anchor instead of
requiring a least time. The translated-increment law is stated for an ordered
additive commutative time monoid with `PartialOrder`, `AddLeftMono`,
`ExistsAddOfLE`, `Sub`, and `OrderedSub`. These assumptions express the two
steps used in the proof: left translation preserves monotone grids, and the
interval from `q` to `r` has length `r - q`. The duration assumptions use
Mathlib's `ExistsAddOfLE` and `OrderedSub` interfaces
([`ExistsAddOfLE`](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/021c46bdd042f67b538b9f9871d556a93713a9a9/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Monoid/Unbundled/ExistsOfLE.lean),
[`OrderedSub`](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/021c46bdd042f67b538b9f9871d556a93713a9a9/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Sub/Defs.lean)).
The theorem uses only independent and stationary increments; no càdlàg,
stochastic-continuity, or stable-law assumption enters its statement. The
rational uniform-block path theorem keeps real-valued path geometry, but
assumes only these two increment properties and coordinate measurability. Its
stable-process corollary remains at the stable small-deviation boundary as an
adapter.

This placement follows the mathematical dependencies rather than the number
of clients: the standalone stationary-increment predicate and state-group
finite-dimensional law are reusable process results, while the rational tube
event remains a real path-space specialization. The comparison also prevents
the stronger `IsLevyProcess` bundle, whose càdlàg component is unused, from
becoming the hypothesis of the generic block-law theorem.

## Abstraction research: finite cyclic-gap expansion

The cross-module use of the finite cyclic-gap formula triggered a review of
its mathematical generality before deciding its placement. Bauer, Godrèche,
and Luck derive the cyclic events, their finite inclusion--exclusion, and the
factorization over consecutive gaps in Appendix A, equations (A.3)--(A.6),
of *Statistics of persistent events in the binomial random walk: Will the
drunken sailor hit the sober man?* ([arXiv:cond-mat/9905252](https://arxiv.org/abs/cond-mat/9905252),
*Journal of Statistical Physics* 96 (1999), 963--1019,
DOI 10.1023/A:1004636216365). The paper presents the calculation for a
one-dimensional random walk. The Lean proof was checked against these exact
finite event identities; the broader state-space statement below is a
generalization inferred from the proof's hypotheses, not a claim attributed
to Bauer--Godrèche--Luck.

The repository's Mathlib dependency is pinned at
`380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51`. In that revision, the order
interface is expressed by `[AddCommGroup G] [LinearOrder G]
[IsOrderedAddMonoid G]`; the former bundled name `LinearOrderedAddCommGroup`
does not exist there. The relevant definitions are in the pinned
[Mathlib ordered-group source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51/Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Group/Defs.lean).
For measurability, the pinned
[Mathlib group-arithmetic source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Group/Arithmetic.lean)
provides `MeasurableAdd₂`. No cyclic-survival or cyclic-gap identity was
found in the corresponding Mathlib probability modules; the finite-sum and
coordinate-permutation ingredients are assembled from the existing algebra
and finite-product APIs.

The audit distinguishes the assumptions needed at each step. The finite
partial-sum identities use an additive commutative group. The cyclic cover
uses a minimum among finitely many partial sums, so its present proof uses a
linear order compatible with addition. The probability argument additionally
uses measurability of addition and an explicit hypothesis that
`Set.Ici (0 : G)` is measurable. Measurability of subtraction is not needed:
a rotated survival event is identified with the preimage of ordinary
survival under a coordinate permutation, which is measurable independently
of subtraction on `G`. This makes the published cyclic-gap theorem's
assumptions weaker than the first proof draft's assumptions.

The complete cyclic-gap expansion is a meaningful result in its own right,
so it is exposed as
`Probability/Process/RandomWalk/Fluctuation/SparreAndersen/Composition/CyclicGapSum.lean`.
Its statement covers iid increments valued in any linearly ordered measurable
additive commutative group satisfying the hypotheses above. The generic
finite cyclic-gap construction and marked-composition reindexing are in
`Combinatorics/Sequence/CyclicGap/{Basic,Reindex}.lean`; the real-valued
positive-composition identity remains a specialization in
`Composition/EndpointProbability.lean`. Event descriptions and
block-factorization steps stay under `Composition/Lemmas/`, because they encode
the particular cyclic events and assemble this expansion. Their use by the
public theorem is not, by itself, a reason to externalize them.

## Abstraction research: consecutive IID blocks and finite products

The coordinate-block independence declarations formerly in
`Probability/Process/RandomWalk/Path/Block/Law/Coordinates.lean` used only the
canonical IID sequence law, coordinate extraction, and cumulative block
lengths. They required no random-walk path, addition, or moment hypotheses,
so they now live in `Probability/Sequence/IID/Blocks/Consecutive.lean` under
`ProbabilityTheory`. Default-valued finite-block measurability likewise moved
from the random-walk path layer to `Probability/Sequence/Block.lean`.
Random-walk block sums and path-event consequences remain with
`RandomWalk/Path/Block/Law/`.

The pinned Mathlib revision is
`380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51`. Mathlib provides
[`Measure.pi_pi`](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Constructions/Pi.html)
for evaluating product measures on measurable rectangles and
`Measure.pi_map_piCongrLeft` for reindexing finite coordinate products; the
pinned source is
[`Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Constructions/Pi.lean`](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Constructions/Pi.lean).
These are the broad measure-theoretic interfaces. The consecutive IID block
theorems add the useful sequence-level specialization: arbitrary measurable
events on disjoint blocks factor under the canonical IID law.

The pinned Mathlib probability API also has the still more general
`iIndepFun.indepFun_finset` theorem: if $(X_i)_{i\in I}$ is an independent
family and finite index sets $S,T\subseteq I$ are disjoint, then the tuples
$(X_i)_{i\in S}$ and $(X_i)_{i\in T}$ are independent. Its statement accepts
an arbitrary index type and coordinate-dependent value types; see the
[official API documentation](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Probability/Independence/Basic.html)
and the pinned
[`Independence/Basic.lean`](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51/Mathlib/Probability/Independence/Basic.lean#L795).
Thus the local two-block coordinate-independence theorem remains an IID
sequence adapter using `blockCoordinates`, while a new arbitrary-finite-set
independence theorem would duplicate Mathlib's API. The mutual-independence
and event-factorization results for variable-length consecutive blocks retain
their sequence-level value: they package the cumulative block starts and
identify every block-event probability with the corresponding origin-block
probability under one common marginal law.

The finite-product adapter formerly exposed from
`RandomWalk/Path/Block/Law/FiniteProduct.lean` has only one client, the cyclic
gap factorization in Bauer--Godrèche--Luck, Appendix A, equation (A.6). Its
proof identifies the cyclic gaps with consecutive blocks, then uses the
Mathlib product-rectangle and reindexing APIs. That adapter does not define a
second reusable probability interface, so its two declarations are now
`private lemma`s inside
`RandomWalk/Fluctuation/SparreAndersen/Composition/Lemmas/BlockProbability/IIDFactorization.lean`,
beside the proof that consumes them. The one-use two-block prefix adapter was
also removed: its bridge and finite-cover clients now call the more general
`Probability/Sequence/IID/Blocks/Prefix.lean` theorem, which accepts any event
measurable from the finite prefix.

The pinned Mathlib source was also checked for a cumulative start-index API.
[`List.ranges` in `Mathlib.Data.List.Range`](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Data/List/Range.html)
constructs pairwise-disjoint ranges from a finite list of lengths and proves
that their concatenation is the range of the total length. It is appropriate
for a finite list, while the IID block interface is parameterized by an
arbitrary function `length : ℕ → ℕ`. No Mathlib declaration directly gives the
prefix sum `b_j = \sum_{i<j} length(i)` for that interface. This index-only
construction and its recurrence/monotonicity laws therefore now belong to
`Combinatorics.Sequence.Block` as `Combinatorics.Sequence.blockStart`; it has
no state-space, algebra, or probability assumptions. There is no
`AdditivePath.blockStart` forwarding declaration; consumers use the sequence
module's definition and recurrence laws directly.

Mathlib's product-measure API already supplies the more abstract mechanisms:
[`Measure.pi_pi`, `Measure.pi_map_piCongrLeft`, and
`measurePreserving_sumPiEquivProdPi`](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Constructions/Pi.html).
These handle measurable rectangles, coordinate reindexing, and decomposition
of products over a sum of index types. The cyclic-gap product calculation is
therefore kept private in its one proof chain instead of introducing another
public finite-product theorem.

The directory count review excluded vendored and test trees. The three
production directories with eight direct Lean modules are `Kernel/Killed/Return`,
`Path/Skorokhod/Corridor/UniformBlocks`, and
`Distributions/Stable/Attraction/Norming`. Their modules state distinct
return-kernel, uniform-block, and norming interfaces; they have no shared
theorem-specific proof family that would make another subdirectory clearer.
They remain grouped under these semantic owners. A scan of the production tree
found no same-level `.lean` file and directory with the same stem. Repeated
short filenames such as `Basic.lean` in different semantic subdirectories
remain appropriate: Mathlib uses the same local naming pattern throughout its
subject-organized source tree.

The pinned Mathlib tree also contains 775 `Basic.lean` modules, 73
`Lemmas.lean` modules, and one `Theorems.lean` module, with no
`Definitions.lean` module. Reusing a short filename in distinct semantic
directories is therefore an established Mathlib pattern; the full module path
provides the identity. This project keeps the stricter local rule against a
same-parent `Foo.lean` and `Foo/` pair for discoverability, while retaining
short names such as `Basic.lean` and concept-specific nested `Lemmas/` where
their owners are clear. The count was recomputed directly from the pinned
source at Mathlib revision `380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51`.

## Abstraction review: stable finite-variation entrance positivity (2026-10-19)

The finite-variation Poisson construction had been stored as
`Probability/Process/Stable/JumpModel/EntranceLaw.lean`, even though its
conclusion is positivity of the stable small-deviation event
`fullSegmentCorridorReturnEvent`. This made the reusable jump-model directory
depend on a small-deviation event. The result now lives at
`Stable/SmallDeviation/Blocks/Lower/Entrance/PoissonModel.lean`, and its public
theorem is
`IsStableLevyProcess.measure_fullEntrance_pos_indexLTOne`:

```lean
(h : IsStableLevyProcess α μ X P) → α < 1 →
(0 < cdf μ 0 ∧ cdf μ 0 < 1) → -1 < b ∧ b < 1 → -1 < c ∧ c < 1 →
0 < ε → 0 < P (fullSegmentCorridorReturnEvent X 0 1
  (c - 1) (c + 1) (c - b - ε) (c - b + ε))
```

The proof-only statement with an explicit
`LevyKhintchineTriple`, `SigmaFinite` instance, and characteristic-function
identity is now a private lemma in that module. Strict stability already
provides such a triple, so including it in the public theorem's assumptions
would expose a proof representation rather than the mathematical condition.
The narrower half-open endpoint wrapper and four scaled/log-ratio wrappers
in `ShiftComparison/PoissonEntrance.lean` had no callers beyond their own
adapter chain; the scaled form is already supplied by the stable scaling API,
and the other wrappers were removed with that unused chain. The all-index
entrance statement remains the only entry in `ShiftComparison/AllIndices.lean`.

The abstraction review compared three levels. First, the pinned Mathlib
revision is `380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51`; its
[`map_eq_iff_forall_finset_map_restrict_eq`](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51/Mathlib/Probability/Process/FiniteDimensionalLaws.lean)
states that equality of all finite-dimensional distributions is equivalent
to equality of process laws for almost-everywhere measurable process maps
under a finite measure. Second, the repository's
`HasIndepIncrements.process_identDistrib_of_aemeasurable` is a cross-space
process-law theorem: zero starts, independent increments, and matching
increment distributions imply equality of the process laws. These are the
general law-transfer ingredients used by the Poisson proof; they already live
at their general process-law layer.

Third, the repository's path-space support theorem accepts an arbitrary
probability measure on `CadlagPath unitInterval ℝ`: if the straight path to
`c-b` belongs to its support, then the corresponding open corridor and
terminal window have positive joint probability. This is more abstract than
the stable adapter, and remains in the path/support layer. Thomas Simon's
“Petites déviations et support d'un processus de Lévy,” *Comptes Rendus de
l'Académie des Sciences*, Série I 329(4) (1999), 331--334, DOI
[10.1016/S0764-4442(00)88576-6](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0764-4442(00)88576-6),
and its expanded treatment “On the small deviations of a Lévy process,”
*Potential Analysis* 14 (2001), 155--173, DOI
[10.1023/A:1008711917156](https://doi.org/10.1023/A:1008711917156), characterize
small-deviation support and the support of Lévy laws in Skorokhod space. This
is a possible route to a broader Lévy-process support interface, but it does
not by itself identify the present prescribed nonzero terminal window from
the CDF sign condition. The finite-variation construction supplies that
specific implication. Therefore the general law-transfer and path-support
results stay public at their existing abstract layers, while the stable
entrance theorem stays with its small-deviation event. Cross-module use was
only the audit trigger; the placement follows these mathematical interfaces.

## Abstraction review: uniform-block feedback probabilities (2026-10-19)

The former `Stable/SmallDeviation/Blocks/Factorization.lean` contained two
theorems whose proofs used only independent increments, stationary increments,
coordinate measurability, and the rational uniform-block event interface.
Neither conclusion used a stable law. The finite product lower bound now lives
in `Probability/Process/Path/Skorokhod/Corridor/UniformBlocks/Probability/Bounds.lean`
as
`HasIndepIncrements.pow_le_measure_rationalUniformPrefixBlockEvent`:

```lean
(h : HasIndepIncrements X P) → HasStationaryIncrements X P →
(∀ t, AEMeasurable (fun ω => X t ω) P) → MeasurableSet V →
q ≤ P (block 0 ∈ V) →
q ^ blocks ≤ P (every translated uniform block lies in V)
```

This is the weakest process interface used by the formal proof; it does not
assume zero start, càdlàg paths, stability, a moment condition, or a scaling
law. The stable finite-time entrance argument supplies its process facts and
one-block estimate at the application boundary.

The abstraction comparison checked pinned Mathlib revision
`380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51`. Its
[`iIndepFun.measure_inter_preimage_eq_mul`](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51/Mathlib/Probability/Independence/Basic.lean)
is stronger at the measure-theoretic level: for an arbitrary finite family of
independent random variables and measurable coordinate events, it gives the
exact finite-product identity, including a different event for each index.
The repository's
`HasIndepIncrements.iIndepFun_rationalUniformBlocks` and
`HasIndepIncrements.rationalUniformBlockProcess_identDistrib` provide the
path-process independence and stationarity specializations. The new theorem
packages these process facts into the complete lower bound for the existing
uniform-prefix event. Its common event `V` matches that event's meaning; for
different measurable events at each block, the general Mathlib product
identity is the more abstract endpoint and requires no additional local
wrapper.

The other former declaration,
`IsStableLevyProcess.measure_prefixTube_inter_nextBlock`, was a single-use
stable receiver around
`HasIndepIncrements.indepFun_rationalPrefix_nextBlock` followed by
`IndepFun.measure_inter_preimage_eq_mul`. It was removed; the upper-bound
proof now applies those general APIs directly. Thus the former
`Blocks/Factorization.lean` file was deleted rather than retaining a
stable-specific public facade. The repository's generic
`measure_adaptiveChoice_ge_mul` likewise already states the binary feedback
inequality for arbitrary independent past and future maps; the path-level
feedback module applies it to rational block paths, and its public interface
now assumes only independent increments and coordinate measurability.

## Abstraction review: finite-choice block feedback (2026-10-19)

`Stable/SmallDeviation/Blocks/Lower/Binning/Basic.lean` also contained the
one-step estimate `IsStableLevyProcess.measure_prefixBin_nextBlock_ge_mul`.
Its proof used only the finite-partition measure inequality,
`HasIndepIncrements.indepFun_rationalPrefix_nextBlock`, and coordinate
measurability. The stable-law assumption supplied only the last item. The
three lower-block consumers in `Return/Basic.lean` and
`Assembly/Concatenation.lean` now call
`HasIndepIncrements.measure_rationalPrefixFiniteChoiceNextBlock_ge_mul` in the
uniform-block feedback module. Its hypotheses are independent increments,
almost-everywhere measurable coordinates, measurable prefix and next-block
events, pairwise disjoint prefix cells, and a common lower bound for each
cell's next-block event. Its conclusion is the full finite-choice inequality
for rational uniform-block paths; no stationary or stable increment law is
needed. The tube-covering specialization remains in the stable small-deviation
layer because it additionally uses the stable application’s endpoint bins
and coverage statement.

The comparison used pinned Mathlib revision
`380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51`. Mathlib's
[`IndepFun.measure_inter_preimage_eq_mul`](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51/Mathlib/Probability/Independence/Basic.lean)
is the general factorization theorem for two independent random variables
and measurable coordinate events. The repository's
`MeasureTheory.measure_iUnion_inter_ge_mul_of_finite_partition` already
states the measure inequality for arbitrary finite disjoint families, without
assuming independence. Their combination now gives the separate public
`measure_finiteAdaptiveChoice_ge_mul` in `Probability/Independence/AdaptiveChoice.lean`:
for arbitrary measurable past and future spaces, an independent pair of random
variables, a finite disjoint family of past events, and one future event per
cell, the lower bound follows from a common lower bound on the selected future
probabilities. This is a finite-choice theorem with independent use beyond
the path application, and it strictly generalizes the existing binary
feedback principle. The path-level result then applies it to uniform
prefix/next-block maps using `HasIndepIncrements`; it retains the richer
process statement without adding a stable-law assumption. The
[`Mathlib independence documentation`](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Probability/Independence/Basic.html)
and [`independent-increments documentation`](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Probability/Independence/Process/HasIndepIncrements/Basic.html)
confirm the semantics and scope of those interfaces.

`Stable/SmallDeviation/Blocks/Upper/Basic.lean` had an unused public theorem
