## Abstraction review: positive-`a` endpoint PZ chain (2026-10-19)

The proof family had been grouped in a directory named after its parameter
condition rather than the mathematics in the files. It now lives under
`EndpointDeviation/FirstStage/`: the entry proves an
exponential low-count bound for the first-stage killed population, and its
first-stage cutoff itself does not depend on that exponent, so its definition
and scale-property declarations now use the semantic name
`positiveAFirstStageCutoff`.

`EndpointDeviation/FirstStage/Lemmas/PZBudget.lean` estimates the
tilted-spine corridor mass at the specific cutoff
`positiveAFirstStageCutoff`; its only client is `PZAssembly.lean`.
`PZAssembly.lean` combines that rate with the first-stage MRCA pair sum and
cross-child weight. Its resulting PZ-mean lower bound is used by both
`FirstStage/LowCountPower.lean` and
`SecondStage/Roots/CountLowerBound.lean`, which allocates the first-stage bound to
the second-stage root budget. Neither statement is the general
Paley--Zygmund inequality: both contain the selected population's tilted law,
corridor, cutoff, and model-specific pair bound. They therefore remain
theorem-family lemmas under `FirstStage/Lemmas/`; the second-stage use is a
consumer of the first-stage estimate, not a more general mathematical
interface.

The deterministic schedule and its scale properties now live beside their
owner in `FirstStage/Cutoff.lean`. The limit
`logarithmicSmallDeviationScale (positiveAFirstStageCutoff N n) /
logarithmOfSampleSize N n → 1` had been proved independently in
`PZBudget.lean` and `Spine/Corridor.lean`. It is now one named property of the
cutoff used by both stages; it remains at the endpoint-deviation subject level
because it describes this model-specific schedule rather than a general
asymptotic operation.

The pinned Mathlib source at revision
`380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51` has no declaration named for the
Paley--Zygmund inequality. Its general probability-space form had already
been proved in `BranchingProcess/GaltonWatson/Growth.lean`; its location and
namespace were narrower than its assumptions and conclusion. It is now exposed
from `Probability/MeasureTheory/Moments/PaleyZygmund.lean` as
`ProbabilityTheory.measure_ge_threshold_of_moments`: for `X ≥ 0` almost
everywhere, `X ∈ L¹ ∩ L²`, `𝔼[X] = m`, `𝔼[X²] = s > 0`, and `0 ≤ t < m`,
`(m - t)² / s ≤ ℙ(t ≤ X)`. This is the random-variable form of Paley and
Zygmund, [*On some series of functions, (3)*, Lemma 19, p. 192
(1932)](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0305004100010860). The module also contains
the general corollary `measure_ge_threshold_of_secondMoment_le`. The Galton--Watson moment
recurrences and finite-generation specializations remain in `Growth.lean`.

The separate estimate `∫ X² ≤ 2 ∫ X` under `0 ≤ X ≤ 2` had also been exported
from `Growth.lean`, although its only caller was a Boolean test example with
the two moments already computed exactly. Its proof was a direct application
of Mathlib's `integral_mono_ae` after the pointwise inequality `X² ≤ 2X`; the
general integral-order API is documented in
[Mathlib's Bochner integral module](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/Bochner/Basic.html#MeasureTheory.integral_mono_ae).
The specialized wrapper was removed instead of promoted to a new generic
moment API. The test example now rewrites by its exact first and second moment
formulas. This keeps `Growth.lean` focused on Galton--Watson generation
moments and growth estimates, and removes a public declaration missing from
the module's declaration list.

## Galton--Watson growth declaration visibility and module header (2026-10-24)

The public-header and use-site audit of
`Probability/BranchingProcess/GaltonWatson/Growth.lean` found eight
module-local proof-support declarations exposed at the namespace level:
`generationFieldValue`, `generationSizeReal_measurable`,
`generationSizeReal_memLp_two`, `generationSizeReal_integrable`,
`generationFirstMoment_eq_fieldLaw`, `generationSecondMoment_eq_fieldLaw`,
`generationFirstMoment_zero`, and
`rho_pow_sq_le_secondMoment_of_recursion`. None occurs in a public declaration
type or a public definition body, and none has an external client. They are now
private; their use in the proof terms of public theorems remains local to the
module. The 23 remaining module-visible declarations are each listed by exact
name in the opening module docstring with the corresponding moment or
probability formula.

The module no longer imports `Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.Bochner.Set`;
after removing the one-use bounded-variable inequality, its declarations use
the general integral API through the remaining imports. `Growth`,
`BoundedGrowth`, the finite-slot and bounded-offspring downstream modules, and
`BranchingProcessTest/Branching/GaltonWatsonGrowth.lean` elaborate with the
pinned toolchain. Mathlib `lint-style` passes for `Growth`, and
`git diff --check` is clean. This is one completed family in the ongoing
whole-tree review.

The same moment argument has a useful support-event form for an
`ENNReal`-valued observable `X`: if `∫⁻ X = m` and `∫⁻ X² ≤ s` with
`0 < s < ∞`, then `m² / s ≤ μ {ω | X ω ≠ 0}`. A source audit found this
fully generic proof embedded in `Spine/Tube/SecondMoment/OneGenerationTail.lean`;
the only model-specific use is to turn a corridor path-count moment estimate
into the probability that one root has a corridor path. It now lives beside
the real-valued form in `Probability/MeasureTheory/Moments/PaleyZygmund.lean`,
and the path-count theorem imports it as a probability-moments result. This
reuses Mathlib's general `ENNReal` Hölder inequality
([official API](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/MeanInequalities.html));
the pinned Mathlib source supplies that analytic ingredient but has no
Paley--Zygmund theorem. The support-event form is not a duplicate of the
real-valued threshold theorem: it applies directly to extended-nonnegative
path counts and avoids imposing unnecessary real-integrability conversions.

The API review compared this statement with Mathlib's general
[Markov inequality](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/Lebesgue/Markov.lean)
and [(L^2) integral API](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/L2Space.lean).
These supply neighboring ingredients, while the pinned revision has no
Paley--Zygmund theorem; the general probability-space statement is the useful
public abstraction, and the model-specific rate lemmas remain under
`FirstStage/Lemmas/`. Their use in later modules alone does not justify
promoting them. Only the positivity of the corridor probability is consumed
by `FirstStage/LowCountPower.lean`; the bundled corridor lower bound duplicates
the existing PZ estimate, and the trivial drawdown probability bound is proved
directly where it is used. The caller now invokes the existing spine-corridor
positivity theorem. The unused package and its one-declaration
`Population/PZInput.lean` module and import edge are removed.

## Abstraction review: root-indexed Ulam--Harris families (2026-10-19)

The root-indexed tree types in `Combinatorics/UlamHarris/Tree/Defs.lean` and
`MarkedTree/Basic.lean` are aliases for function families:
`RootIndexed.Tree Root α = Root → Tree α` and
`RootIndexed.MarkedTree Root α X = Root → MarkedTree α X`. The first module
also defined a `reindex` operation by `T.reindex f := fun r => T (f r)` and
proved its application, identity, and composition equations. The marked-tree
module repeated the same operation and laws; the only client of that wrapper
was its local mark-forgetting equation.

We compared these candidate APIs with the pinned Mathlib revision
`380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51`. `Function.comp` already states
precomposition at arbitrary function types, with `Function.comp_apply`,
`Function.comp_assoc`, `id_comp`, and `comp_id`; see Mathlib's
[`Logic/Function/Basic.lean`](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51/Mathlib/Logic/Function/Basic.lean)
and [`Logic/Function/Defs.lean`](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51/Mathlib/Logic/Function/Defs.lean),
and the [official function API documentation](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Logic/Function/Defs.html).
The indexed-tree `reindex` declarations added no structure or theorem beyond
that function API and had no independent clients, so they were removed.
Pointwise root, parent, and sibling wrappers were removed for the same reason:
each is obtained directly from the corresponding field of `T r`. The
`FiniteRootTree` and `CountableRootTree` aliases and the finite extensionality
alias had no clients and introduced no additional structure. The single-tree
`Tree.mem_parent` remains because the graph arborescence proof uses its
parent-prefix formulation; `Tree.ext` remains used by the marked-tree and
branching-walk equivalence proofs.

The root-indexed mark-forgetting equation is retained in the more direct form
`forgetMark (M ∘ f) = forgetMark M ∘ f`, as
`RootIndexed.MarkedTree.forgetMark_comp`. This records the naturality of the
semantic projection without defining a tree-specific composition operation.

The related `ProbabilityTheory.BranchingRandomWalk.RootIndexed.StepField`
API was checked against the generic function interfaces in the pinned Mathlib
revision `380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51` and the Lean 4.35.0-rc3
core API, following the cross-module abstraction review rule in
[`CONTRIBUTING.md`](../../CONTRIBUTING.md#lean-module-headers-and-mathematical-references).
For
`step : Root → TreeNode α → Step α X` and
`f : NewRoot × TreeNode α → Root × TreeNode α`, the most general ordinary
function expression for the coordinate pullback is
`Function.curry (Function.uncurry step ∘ f)`. Mathlib's
[`Function.bicompl`](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51/Mathlib/Logic/Function/Defs.lean)
is another candidate, with
`Function.uncurry (Function.bicompl step g h) =
Function.uncurry step ∘ Prod.map g h`; it covers separately reindexed
coordinates but not an arbitrary joint map `f`, where the selected root may
depend on the address. The general candidate is therefore composition after
uncurrying, followed by currying, using Lean's
[`Function.curry` and `Function.uncurry`](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Init/Data/Function.html)
and Mathlib's
[`Function.comp`](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Logic/Function/Defs.html).
These interfaces require no probabilistic, finiteness, or injectivity
assumptions.

The subject-level
`RootIndexed.StepField.reindexCoordinates` remains a named semantic operation
in `Probability/BranchingRandomWalk/Genealogy/RootIndexed/Field/Basic.lean`:
it returns a root-indexed branching step field from an arbitrary map of its
root/address coordinates, and the probability-law and selected-coordinate
interfaces use that field-valued map. Its 50 references across eight modules
confirm those call sites; the count is not the reason to promote it to a more
general layer. The coordinate operation already accepts the weakest natural
assumptions, while a new general pullback declaration would repeat
`Function.comp` together with currying. Accordingly, the unused
`reindexCoordinates_id` and `reindexCoordinates_comp` wrappers were removed;
their content is supplied by the general composition and currying laws. The
root-only `reindex` remains the named specialization for relabelling initial
ancestors and is connected to coordinate pullback by
`reindex_eq_reindexCoordinates`.

## Abstraction review: countable-range coordinate evaluation (2026-10-19)

The dynamic coordinate measurability proofs in
`Probability/BranchingRandomWalk/Tree/Filtration.lean` and
`Probability/BranchingRandomWalk/Genealogy/RootIndexed/Field/Filtration.lean`
had the same measurable-union argument. The pinned Mathlib revision
`380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51` provides
[`Measurable.eval`](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/MeasurableSpace/Constructions.lean#L591)
for one fixed coordinate and
[`Measurable.of_eval`](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/MeasurableSpace/Constructions.lean#L596)
for a function into a full `Pi` space, whose hypothesis gives measurability
at every coordinate. The [official API documentation](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/MeasurableSpace/Constructions.html)
states these same interfaces. Neither covers evaluation at a selector whose
actual range is countable while the ambient index type can be uncountable.

The general useful statement is placed in
`MeasureTheory/MeasurableSpace/CountableEvaluation.lean`:

```text
F : Ω → I → X,  s : Ω → I,
Countable (range s),
∀ i ∈ range s,  Measurable (fun ω => F ω i),
∀ i ∈ range s,  MeasurableSet {ω | s ω = i}
⊢ Measurable (fun ω => F ω (s ω)).
```

The index type `I` has no measurable-space assumption, and the two
measurability hypotheses are required only for indices that can actually be
selected. This is weaker and more reusable than either branching-specific
theorem. The public `Measurable.eval_of_countable_range` proves it by
expressing each preimage as a countable union of the selector fiber
intersected with one coordinate preimage. The two filtration theorems now
specialize this result using their respective depth conditions and measurable
selector fibers. The general theorem belongs in the public measurable-space
layer; the two filtration statements remain public at their semantic owners.
No branching-specific wrapper was moved outward based on its client count.

## Abstraction review: graded-coordinate filtrations (2026-10-19)

The tree-mark filtration and the root-indexed step-field filtration both
reveal a coordinate according to the depth of its address. Their common
mathematical structure is a family of observations `X_i : Ω → E_i` with a
revelation grade `r(i)` in a time preorder:

`𝓕_t = ⨆_{i : I} ⨆_{r(i) ≤ t} MeasurableSpace.comap X_i m_{E_i}`.

The pinned Mathlib revision
`380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51` was checked against three nearby
interfaces. `MeasureTheory.Filtration.natural` uses the same index as both the
observation index and time, and assumes strongly measurable maps into
metrizable Borel spaces. `MeasureTheory.Filtration.piLE` is the canonical
filtration on a product indexed by a preorder, with the coordinate order
itself determining revelation time. `MeasureTheory.filtrationOfSet` generates
a filtration from one event per time. The first two are documented in the
[official Filtration API](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Probability/Process/Filtration.html);
their pinned definitions are in
[`Filtration.lean`](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51/Mathlib/Probability/Process/Filtration.lean#L395)
(`natural`),
[`Filtration.lean`](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51/Mathlib/Probability/Process/Filtration.lean#L494)
(`piLE`), and
[`Filtration.lean`](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51/Mathlib/Probability/Process/Filtration.lean#L230)
(`filtrationOfSet`). None directly gives a family indexed by an arbitrary
`I` whose grades are mapped into an arbitrary time preorder, while retaining
only measurable-space assumptions on the possibly dependent `E_i`.

The coordinate form also preserves the former generator-set presentation:
Mathlib's `MeasurableSpace.comap_eq_generateFrom` identifies each coordinate
comap with the σ-algebra generated by its measurable preimages, and
`MeasurableSpace.generateFrom_iUnion_measurableSet` identifies their supremum
with the σ-algebra generated by the union of those preimages. These identities
are available in the pinned
[`MeasurableSpace.Basic`](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/MeasurableSpace/Basic.lean#L95)
and
[`MeasurableSpace.Defs`](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/MeasurableSpace/Defs.lean#L480)
interfaces.

The resulting reusable API is placed at
`Probability/Process/Filtration/GeneratedByCoordinates.lean`:

* `MeasureTheory.Filtration.generatedByCoordinates` constructs the filtration
  with the displayed formula from any measurable coordinate family with
  possibly dependent codomains and grade map `r : I → T`.
* `MeasureTheory.Filtration.measurable_coordinate_generatedByCoordinates`
  proves that each coordinate is measurable once `r(i) ≤ t`.
* `MeasureTheory.Filtration.generatedByCoordinates_le` characterizes it as
  the least filtration with those coordinate measurability properties.
* `MeasureTheory.Filtration.measurable_to_generatedByCoordinates` proves the
  sufficient direction, and
  `MeasureTheory.Filtration.measurable_iff_coordinates_generatedByCoordinates`
  records the full iff: coordinatewise measurability is necessary by the
  generator maps and sufficient by the universal property of the generated
  σ-algebra.

This abstraction states the shared filtered-information structure and its
minimality, rather than merely deduplicating two `generateFrom` proofs. In the
branching specializations, the grade is `u.length + 1`, so
`u.length < n` is exactly the condition that the coordinate is visible at
generation `n`. The subject modules keep their named `generationFiltration`
and `stepFiltration` interfaces and use the generic API for their measurable
coordinate proofs and root restriction/reindexing maps.

## Abstraction review: conditional event iteration (2026-10-19)

`Probability/Process/Filtration/ConditionalBlocks.lean` is used by the
drawdown, horizontal-tube, and drifted-tube arguments. Its public iteration
theorems concern arbitrary measurable event sequences and filtrations; the
random-walk block events are supplied by callers. This is a complete
conditional-probability estimate at the process-probability layer, rather
than a proof step tied to any one small-deviation argument.

Mathlib's pinned
[`setIntegral_condExp`](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/ConditionalExpectation/Basic.lean#L231)
and its [official conditional-expectation API](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/ConditionalExpectation/Basic.html)
give the integral identity for a general integrable function and a
sub-σ-algebra. They do not provide the finite sequence event intersection or
the resulting product bound. The local one-step event inequality turns that
identity into an intersection-mass bound; the public product theorems then
iterate it under a filtration and conditional indicator bounds.

The probability-measure assumption matches the unscaled product conclusions:
`conditionalBlockIntersection events 0 = Set.univ`, so the induction base
uses `P.real Set.univ = 1`. A finite measure without normalization would need
the factor `P.real Set.univ` on the product side. The abstraction review
therefore keeps the current probability statement and its natural hypotheses;
dropping `IsProbabilityMeasure` alone would make the displayed bounds false.
The theorem already leaves the state space, events, filtration, and numeric
bounds arbitrary, so no random-walk-specific wrapper is promoted to this
layer.

## Abstraction review: finite product reindexing (2026-10-19)

The cyclic-path argument uses Mathlib's
`MeasurableEquiv.piCongrLeft` directly. The former local homogeneous-`Fin n`
alias added no operation beyond that equivalence and was removed. The event
cover estimate for reindexed product measures now lives in
`MeasureTheory/Measure/Pi/FiniteReindexCover.lean`.

The pinned Mathlib revision already has the more general dependent-coordinate
result `Measure.pi_map_piCongrLeft`: it maps a product of a σ-finite family
of measures along a reindexing equivalence to the reindexed product. Its
[official API documentation](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Constructions/Pi.html)
and pinned source
[`Constructions/Pi.lean`](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Constructions/Pi.lean#L745)
show that neither identical marginals nor probability normalization are
required for product reindexing. The local set-preimage equality merely
rewrapped that theorem and had no clients outside its defining module, so it
is private. The public finite-cover result applies to a family
`ν : ι → Measure E` whenever each coordinate reindexing preserves that
family, with only coordinatewise sigma-finiteness. The generic finite-cover
step itself remains in `MeasureTheory/OuterMeasure/Finite/Cover.lean`.

## Abstraction review: finite-cover outer-measure bounds (2026-10-19)

The cross-module cover arguments were compared with the pinned Mathlib API at
revision `380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51`. Mathlib's
[`OuterMeasure.Basic` API](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/OuterMeasure/Basic.html)
defines an outer measure on `Set Ω → ℝ≥0∞` without a measurable-space
structure, and provides `measure_mono` and
`measure_biUnion_finset_le` for any `OuterMeasureClass`. The two finite-cover
statements therefore use the weaker semantic structure directly:

- If `event ⊆ ⋃ k ∈ cover, rotate k ⁻¹' safe` and each such preimage has the
  same outer measure as `safe`, then
  `μ event ≤ cover.card • μ safe`.
- If `U ⊆ ⋃ i ∈ F, A i`, every cell has a subset `A i ∩ B i ⊆ T`, and
  `c * μ (A i) ≤ μ (A i ∩ B i)`, then
  `c * μ U ≤ F.card * μ T`.

These are generic finite-cover operations, rather than probability-specific
results: neither requires measurable sets, a probability normalization, nor a
particular finite index type. The first statement supports the product
reindexing corollary in
`MeasureTheory/Measure/Pi/FiniteReindexCover.lean`; the second supported the
IID finite-prefix bridge comparison, then housed in
`Probability/Process/RandomWalk/Path/Block/Corridor/Comparison.lean` and now
owned by `Probability/Sequence/IID/Blocks/FiniteCover.lean` (see the
2026-10-26 ownership pass below).
The finite subadditivity step is already Mathlib's
`measure_biUnion_finset_le`, so this module adds only the useful finite-cover
consequences and does not duplicate the underlying outer-measure API. The
statements live at `MeasureTheory/OuterMeasure/Finite/Cover.lean`, their
semantic owner, instead of the former probability-measure-oriented
`MeasureTheory/Measure/Finite/Cover.lean` path.

The API comparison is documented in the official documentation above; its
source is pinned at
[`OuterMeasure/Basic.lean`](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/OuterMeasure/Basic.lean#L80).

## Same-basename module and directory review (2026-10-19)

The first-party Lean source tree has no sibling pairs of the form `Foo.lean`
and `Foo/`, and no direct child file repeats its parent directory in its
basename. The test modules formerly named `TruncationMoments`,
`TruncationSecondMoment`, `BranchingWalkLaw`, `RandomWalkPathLaw`, and
`EndpointDeviationParameters` now use names relative to their directories.
The pinned Mathlib source does use same-basename pairs intentionally; the
`Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.Dirac` entry module re-exports
`Dirac.Def` and `Dirac.Basic`, as shown in the
[official module documentation](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Measure/Dirac.html).
The repository follows the same distinction: a substantive entry module may
sit beside its component directory; an import-only duplicate is removed, and
component files use names relative to their semantic directory. The Mathlib
pattern is an intentional umbrella-module design, not a reason to mechanically
rename local modules or a basis for claiming that Mathlib has no such pairs.

## Abstraction review: convergence interfaces (2026-10-19)

The review started with the probability-measure convergence wrappers and
also checked the existing weak-convergence independence interface. Cross-module
use was treated as a reason to search for the mathematical abstraction, rather
than as the placement criterion.

`Measure.map_eq_of_ae_pointwise_limit` concerns a finite Borel measure and
measurable self-maps; it does not use probability normalization or random
variables. Its owner is therefore `MeasureTheory/Measure/Convergence`, and the
module now lives at `MeasureTheory/Measure/Convergence/MapInvariance.lean`.
The pinned Mathlib API has no direct closure theorem for invariant measures
under almost-everywhere pointwise limits. Its
[`HasOuterApproxClosed` API](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Measure/HasOuterApproxClosed.html)
provides uniqueness of finite Borel measures from bounded continuous test
functions, while dominated convergence provides convergence of their
integrals. The local theorem combines those general ingredients to prove the
invariance conclusion. This comparison was checked against Mathlib revision
`380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51`, including
[`HasOuterApproxClosed.lean`](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Measure/HasOuterApproxClosed.lean)
and the official documentation above.

The weak-convergence review found that
`Probability/ConvergenceInDistribution/Independence.lean` already contains the
forward direction: independent coordinates with convergent marginal laws give
joint convergence to independent limits. The converse closure theorem,
`ProbabilityTheory.indepFun_of_tendstoInDistribution_pair`, now lives beside
it. It allows source spaces and laws to vary with the index, assumes each pair
has independent coordinates, and concludes independence of the limit from
joint-law convergence. The two directions form one coherent finite-product
interface; this placement follows the mathematical subject, not the number of
clients. The proof uses continuity of `ProbabilityMeasure.prod` and Mathlib's
characterization of independence by equality of the joint law with the product
law. The pinned APIs are
[`MeasureTheory.TendstoInDistribution.continuous_comp`](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/ConvergenceInDistribution.html),
[`ProbabilityMeasure.continuous_prod`](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Measure/ProbabilityMeasure.html),
and
[`indepFun_iff_map_prod_eq_prod_map_map`](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Probability/Independence/Basic.html).
Mathlib's `tendstoInDistribution_of_ae_tendsto` supplies the joint-law
convergence in the Brownian first-passage application. This audit used the
online Mathlib documentation and pinned source at revision
`380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51`.

The former `ProbabilityTheory.tendsto_integral_of_eLpNorm_one_sub_const` was
removed because no module used it and Mathlib already proves the stronger
`MeasureTheory.tendsto_integral_of_L1'`: convergence in `L¹` to an arbitrary
integrable function implies convergence of its Bochner integrals, for general
measures and complete normed codomains. The local probability/real/constant
statement was only a specialization. See the pinned
[`Bochner.Basic.lean`](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/Bochner/Basic.lean)
and its [official documentation](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/Bochner/Basic.html).

### Polynomial tails and logarithmic fourth moments

`L2FromPolynomialTails.lean` now states the moment-growth exponent as an
arbitrary real `q`: if the fourth moments are eventually bounded by
`C * (1 + (log n)^q)` and each fixed two-sided tail is bounded by a possibly
different polynomial rate, then the second moments tend to zero. The previous
fixed exponent `8` reflected one application rather than the mathematical
criterion, so the API now exposes the full real-exponent form.

The closest broader Mathlib theorem is the Vitali criterion
`MeasureTheory.tendstoInMeasure_iff_tendsto_Lp_finite`: for a finite measure
and `1 ≤ p < ∞`, convergence in measure together with uniform integrability
is equivalent to convergence in `Lᵖ`. It is more abstract, but it takes
uniform integrability and convergence in measure as inputs rather than the
explicit polynomial-tail and fourth-moment hypotheses used here. The project
therefore keeps the checkable tail-to-`L²` criterion, with its final step
factored through the more general local interface
`ProbabilityTheory.tendsto_integral_sq_of_tendsto_fourthTailControl` in
`L2FromTails.lean`.

The real exponent is supported by Mathlib's
`isLittleO_log_rpow_rpow_atTop`, which proves
`(log x)^q = o(x^p)` for every real `q` and every `p > 0`. This was checked in
the pinned Mathlib revision `380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51`,
[`Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Asymptotics.lean`](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Asymptotics.lean#L365), and against the official
[API documentation](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Asymptotics.html). The Vitali comparison uses the pinned
[`MeasureTheory/Function/UniformIntegrable.lean`](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/UniformIntegrable.lean#L566)
and its [official documentation](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/UniformIntegrable.html).

`Mogulskii/Stable/TruncatedMoment.lean` used only a probability measure,
truncated moments, and the distributional norming factor $L^*$; its theorem
statements had no walk, path, or small-deviation hypotheses. It therefore
belongs with the stable norming definition rather than under the random-walk
small-deviation development. The module now lives at
`Probability/Distributions/Stable/Attraction/Norming/Asymptotics/TruncatedMoment.lean`,
beside the tail and norming results, and the stable-attraction test imports
that owner. The fully general truncated-moment identities remain in
`Probability/Distributions/Moments/Truncated/Basic.lean`; the moved results
are the stable-factor specializations $L^*(u)\to A-B$ and
$L^*(u)\to\alpha B/(2-\alpha)$ under their respective tail limits.

The identity `IsStableLevyProcess.unitIntervalPathLaw_spatialScale` was also
inside `TerminalLeft/Normalization.lean`. Its proof only needed an
almost-surely càdlàg real process, so that stable-process wrapper was removed
and the reusable theorem `pathLaw_smul` was added to
`Probability/Process/Path/Representation/Cadlag.lean`. It states
`pathLaw(P, qX) = (pathLaw(P, X)).map (scalePath q)` for every real `q`.
`PathLaw/UnitInterval.lean` now owns only the stable-process path-law
construction and stable-clock results. The one-use coefficient substitution
`sourceNormalization` is private in the terminal-left normalization module;
the exported raw-normalization theorem remains there.

The public abstraction reviewed for this move is: for any real process
`X : unitInterval → Ω → ℝ` with `AEMeasurable (X t) P` at every time and
almost-surely càdlàg paths, and any `q : ℝ`,
`pathLaw(P, qX) = (pathLaw(P, X)).map (scalePath q)`. No probability,
independent-increment, stable-law, or positivity assumption on `q` is needed.
The pinned Mathlib source at revision
[`380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51`](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/tree/380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51)

Mathlib supplies these measure-map operations but has no `CadlagPath` path-law
API; the reusable path-law statement therefore belongs in the project's

The module headers in `Stable/Scale/Rate.lean`,
`Stable/RandomWalkBounds/Partition/{EnergyUpper,Upper}.lean`, and

declarations and quantitative conclusions. These are candidate-list fixes

## Fixed endpoint-window parameter selection (2026-10-21)

The fixed `α = 2` endpoint-window selection in
`Mogulskii/Rate/Endpoint/Selection/Lemmas/FixedParameters.lean` is a proof
assembly for one rate argument. Its floor sequences depend together on the
spectral constant, the selected lattice proportion, the endpoint mesh, and
the application lower bound. The cross-module estimate records exactly the
result needed by `Endpoint/Selection/Basic.lean`; exporting the intermediate
integer sequences or a record packaging these four parameters would expose
the implementation choices rather than a separate reusable probability
statement.

The reusable rounding operation is already
`Asymptotics.floorBlockLength`, with general convergence and quotient results
in `Analysis/Asymptotics/Scale/Block/Length.lean`. The scale hypothesis is
`IsMogulskiiScale`, whose meaning is `x_n → ∞` and `x_n / √n → 0`. The
fixed-parameter module therefore remains under the nested `Lemmas/` directory;
the semantic scale and floor APIs remain with their broader owners. Its module
header now states the assumptions of the cross-module estimate, including the
Brownian realization regularity and each strict parameter margin, rather than
describing the application lower bound as a return probability. This review
follows Mathlib's location checklist: search for a more general existing
result, choose the semantic owner, and assess whether an API has future use
beyond its current caller
([Mathlib review guide](https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/pr-review.html#location-location)).

## Gaussian product-parameter helper module review (2026-10-27)

`Gaussian/Blocks/Lemmas/ProductParameters.lean` contains one 162-line
parameter-selection proof for the finite Gaussian partition lower bound. It
chooses a common positive error tolerance and survival lower bound for a finite
family of Gaussian return products. Its sole current caller is
`Mogulskii/Rate/Partition/Finite.lean`, which imports the helper with
`import all`. The plain Lean `section` keeps the declaration inside the package
module rather than exposing it as public API.

A separate module is justified here because the proof is a substantial,
coherent numerical gap-allocation stage: it selects a minimum over the finite
family, transfers the strict gap to a real-valued margin, and distributes that
margin across the block count. A short one-use helper would stay `private` in
its caller; this proof would make the rate-assembly module harder to navigate if
embedded there. Its Gaussian return-product conclusion is specific to this
proof, while Mathlib's `Finset.exists_min_image` and product inequalities
provide the reusable finite-order tools. It therefore belongs under
`Gaussian/Blocks/Lemmas/`, not at a broader public abstraction layer. The
header cites Mogulskii (1974), Theorem 3, Section 4, p. 764. The helper and its
caller compile together.

## Power-law small-deviation scale interface (2026-10-20)

`EndpointDeviation/Rate/LogScales.lean` specialized the predicate
`Asymptotics.IsSmallDeviationScale` to $k^{2/5}$ relative to $\sqrt{k}$ and
proved that instance by repeating the positive- and negative-power limit
arguments. The scale predicate itself is independent of branching processes,
and the natural general statement is $0<p<q$ implying
$(n^p)\to\infty$ and $n^p/n^q\to0$. This is a reusable relation between
power scales, so it belongs in `Analysis/Asymptotics/Scale/`, outside the
branching-random-walk endpoint-deviation subtree.

The new `Analysis/Asymptotics/Scale/Power/SmallDeviation.lean` exposes

Mathlib's `tendsto_rpow_atTop` and `tendsto_rpow_neg_atTop` in
`Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Pow.Asymptotics.lean` (pinned revision
`380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51`): the first gives divergence, and
the second gives the vanishing ratio after
$n^p/n^q=n^{-(q-p)}$ for positive $n$. See the
[pinned Mathlib source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Asymptotics.lean#L37-L52)
and [official API documentation](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Pow/Asymptotics.html).
The `LogScales.lean` module header now lists all ten public definitions and

`SmallDeviation.lean` owns the general power-law small-deviation relation and

The stable block-count module is under `Stable/Lemmas/Partition.lean` because
its production callers are all inside the Mogul'skii proof chain. This
placement follows an abstraction review against the pinned Mathlib revision
`380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51` (Lean `v4.35.0-rc3`). Lean core

rounding inputs used here. The pinned Mathlib source has no `blockCount` or
`blockLength` declaration. The repository's general
`Analysis/Asymptotics/Scale/Block/Count.lean` therefore owns the reusable API:
for any `blockLength : ℕ → ℕ` it defines
`blockCount blockLength n = n / blockLength n`, proves
`blockCount * blockLength ≤ n < (blockCount + 1) * blockLength` for positive
length, and derives

`(blockLength n : ℝ) / n → 0`. It also proves the scale-free composition
\[
  \frac{H_n}{n}\to\tau,\quad \frac{b_n}{n}\to0,\quad
  \frac{t_n}{b_n}\to L
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  \frac{t_n}{n}\left\lfloor\frac{H_n}{b_n}\right\rfloor\to L\tau,
\]
for any eventually positive integer block length `b_n`, integer horizon
`H_n`, and real scale `t_n`. This has no probability or stable-law
hypotheses, so it is the reusable interface. The stable module combines it
with Mogul'skii's stable block length
and slow-variation limits to obtain the source-specific value
`stableScaleTime * stableBlockCount / n → 1 / constant`; the bridge-count
consequence remains a proof-chain step, not an independent API.
The unused stable-named wrappers for generic quotient/remainder bounds and
the floor-selected partition-cell specialization were removed; clients use
`Asymptotics`' block-count results or the general segment-count limit directly.
The stable-specific count definition `stableBlockCount` and its asymptotic
limits belong in `Stable/Scale/BlockCount.lean`; the block argument, integer
block length, and their limits belong in `Stable/Scale/BlockLength.lean`. The
extra endpoint-core bridge count remains in the `Lemmas/` subtree as a
proof-chain result. The unused stable-specific slow-diagonal wrapper was removed:
the general selector is in `Analysis/Asymptotics/Scale/SlowDiagonal.lean`, and
the stable-scale choice actually used by the proof is in `Stable/Scale/Basic.lean`.

Sources checked: Lean core's
[`Init.Data.Nat.Div.Basic`](https://lean-lang.org/doc/api/Init/Data/Nat/Div/Basic.html);
Mathlib's
[`Mathlib.Analysis.SpecificLimits.Basic`](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecificLimits/Basic.html);
Mathlib's official asymptotics documentation describes generic limit algebra,
but no block-count composition theorem;
[`Mathlib.Analysis.Asymptotics.Defs`](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Analysis/Asymptotics/Defs.html)
and [`Mathlib.Analysis.Asymptotics.SpecificAsymptotics`](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Analysis/Asymptotics/SpecificAsymptotics.html)
were checked for existing APIs before adding the scale-free composition;
the exact pinned implementation in
[`Analysis/Asymptotics/Scale/Block/Count.lean`](../../Analysis/Asymptotics/Scale/Block/Count.lean)
and the current stable-scale API in
[`Stable/Scale/BlockCount.lean`](../../Probability/Process/RandomWalk/SmallDeviation/Mogulskii/Stable/Scale/BlockCount.lean).

fact: if $f$ injectively relabels candidates and preserves the strict order
of their `valueKey`s, then
`IsFirstNBy N value C S` implies
`IsFirstNBy N targetValue (f '' C) (S.image f)`. This is an invariant of the
abstract finite-or-infinite first-$N$ selection specification, not a
branching-walk construction, so it now lives as

``Combinatorics/BranchingWalk/Selection/`NSelection/Mechanism/Infinite.lean`.

modules now list their public declarations and formulas in their module
headers. The theorem module, trajectory module, and direct clients built with
the pinned toolchain (3,428 Lake jobs); Mathlib `lint-style` passed on the two
edited modules.

## Finite-interval Rademacher model ownership (2026-10-21)

The former `Mogulskii/Spectral/Kernel/Interval.lean`,
`Mogulskii/Spectral/Kernel/Killed.lean`, and
`Mogulskii/Spectral/Survival/Path.lean` defined the concrete finite-interval
walk, not Mogulskii-specific estimates. They now live in
`Probability/Process/RandomWalk/Rademacher/FiniteInterval/{Matrix,KilledKernel,Path}.lean`
under `ProbabilityTheory.RandomWalk.Rademacher.FiniteInterval`. The related
sine-mode decomposition, finite-interval path survival, target expansion,
extremal-pair estimate, and target-mass lower bounds also moved under that
owner, in its `Spectral/` subtree. The former mixed target lower-bound module
was split: finite-time estimates are in
`FiniteInterval/Spectral/Target/LowerBound.lean`, while the diffusive-limit
assembly is in `FiniteInterval/Spectral/Target/DiffusiveLower.lean`. The
finite-interval model is
the killed simple symmetric walk on sites $1,\ldots,N$, with
$K_N(i,j)=\frac12\mathbf1_{j=i-1}+\frac12\mathbf1_{j=i+1}$ for interior
neighbors, and survival event
$\{1\le x+S_j\le N\text{ for }1\le j\le n\}$. Its sine eigenfunction and
the identification of its kernel mass with IID path survival are independent
of the Mogulskii scaling argument. The return-kernel estimates transferred
from the Brownian corridor are independent of a Mogulskii scale, so their
owner is `HorizontalTube/Kernel/DiffusiveReturnLower.lean`. The finite IID
block comparisons for horizontal tubes likewise have no scale or moment
assumption and are owned by `HorizontalTube/Blocks/UpperBound.lean`; the strict
whole-path range inequality is in `Range/IndependentBlocks.lean`. Mogulskii's
endpoint-band and partition constructions remain under
`Mogulskii/RandomWalkBounds/`. This keeps the spectral directory focused on
finite-interval eigenfunction arguments and their Mogulskii asymptotics.

The abstraction audit compared these declarations with Mathlib at the pinned
Mathlib revision `380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51`. Mathlib's
[`Matrix.rowStochastic`](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Stochastic.html)
requires each row sum to equal one, whereas killing at the boundary makes the
edge rows substochastic. Mathlib's `ProbabilityTheory.Kernel` supplies the
measure-valued kernel interface but not this finite-interval Rademacher
construction. The repository's reusable `Matrix.IsRowSubstochastic`,
`Kernel.ofRealMatrix`, and bounded-eigenfunction row-sum estimates already
provide the abstract layer; these moved modules supply its concrete
Rademacher specialization without duplicating or promoting that abstraction.
The coefficient identity is part of the generic target interface because it
applies to every finite target. The geometric-error absorption inequality is
used only in the target-mass proof and is private in its defining module.
Mogulskii clients import the finite-interval model from its semantic owner,
and import the diffusive principal-eigenvalue limit directly where their
proofs use it. All 32 changed Lean modules built successfully (3,594 Lake
jobs); the four obsolete empty Mogulskii spectral directories were removed.

## Abstraction review: Lévy–Khintchine exponent and sinc bounds (2026-10-21)

This review checked candidate interfaces against the pinned Mathlib revision
`380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51`, the official
[Mathlib review guidance](https://github.com/leanprover-community/leanprover-community.github.io/blob/lean4/templates/contribute/pr-review.md),
and the official [`Real.sinc` API](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Trigonometric/Sinc.html).
The review guidance asks whether a result is already available in a more
general form and whether the proposed interface remains useful beyond its
current proof. Mathlib provides `Real.sinc`, its continuity, symmetry,
unit bounds, and an inverse-absolute-value bound; the pinned [trigonometric
bounds API](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Trigonometric/Bounds.html)
also provides `Real.sin_ge_sub_cube` and the cosine estimate used below.
The pinned source has no symmetric exponential-average identity for `Real.sinc`
and no two-sided comparison of `1 - Real.sinc x` with `min 1 (x ^ 2)`.

The four sinc statements now live at
`Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Trigonometric/SincBounds.lean`: for real `x`,
`(2 / (3π²)) · min(1,x²) ≤ 1 - Real.sinc x ≤ 2 · min(1,x²)`;
the module also records
`(1/2) ∫_{-1}^1 exp(iux) du = Real.sinc x` and strict positivity away from
zero. The existing Mathlib `Real.sinc` is reused directly. These statements
are standalone real-analysis and Fourier-integral facts, and the bounds are
the general comparison needed for Lévy measures; none mentions a Lévy triple,
an infinitely divisible law, or the smearing construction. Keeping them at the
trigonometric analysis layer makes the estimates available to later analytic
uses without exporting the proof-specific compactness and uniqueness steps.
The small-argument upper-bound proof now uses Mathlib's stronger
`Real.sin_ge_sub_cube` estimate instead of the local exponential Taylor bound.

The exponent `ψ_T(ξ) = ibξ - σ²ξ²/2 + ∫(e^{ixξ} - 1 - ixξ·1_{|x|<1}) dν(x)`
has moved to `LevyKhintchine/Defs.lean` beside its data structure. It is the
definition attached to a triple and is required by the independent scaling
module; the continuity, conditional-negative-definiteness, and representation
proofs remain in `Representation.lean`. Accordingly, `Scaling.lean` imports
`Defs.lean` rather than the full representation proof. `Uniqueness.lean`
imports `Defs`, the sinc-analysis interface, and the characteristic-function
and interval-integral APIs that its public statements expose; it keeps the
representation proof as an ordinary import because it is used only in proofs.
After this narrower import boundary exposed two proof-only dependencies in
downstream modules, `FiniteVariation.lean` and `Stable/Exponent/Basic.lean`
now import those dependencies directly. All seven affected modules pass
`lint-style`, and the full `lake build BranchingProcess` succeeds with 5,602
Lake jobs.

## Abstraction review: conditional positive definiteness and Schoenberg (2026-10-21)

This review compared the candidate interface with A. S. Holevo,
“Conditionally Positive Definite Functions in Quantum Probability,”
*Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians* (Berkeley, 1986),
vol. 2, pp. 1011–1020. The opening paragraph of the Introduction states the group
Schoenberg correspondence: for a complex function `ψ` on a group, `g ↦ exp(tψ(g))`
is positive definite for every `t ≥ 0` exactly when `ψ` is Hermitian and conditionally
positive definite. The proceedings scan is at
<https://sites.math.rutgers.edu/~zeilberg/akherim/icm1986.pdf>; the correspondence is
in the opening paragraph rather than a numbered theorem. Mathlib's review guidance
asks reviewers to check for an existing more-general interface and whether a new
declaration would be useful beyond its current caller
(<https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/pr-review.html>, “Do the results
already exist?” and “Is it formalizing something from the literature?”).

The pinned Mathlib revision `380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51` contains
`Matrix.PosSemidef.hadamard` in `Mathlib.Analysis.Matrix.Order`, the positive
semidefinite Schur product theorem, but no function-level conditionally-positive-definite
API. The repository's `Analysis/Fourier/PositiveDefinite.lean` already supplies the
function-level positive-definite interface on `AddGroup`; that is the matching owner
for the new `Analysis/Fourier/ConditionallyPositiveDefinite/Basic.lean` interface.
Its condition is the full ordered-complex statement
`0 ≤ ∑ i j, conj (c i) * c j * ψ (x i - x j)` for all finite weights with `∑ i, c i = 0`.
Under `ComplexOrder`, this requires the quadratic form to be real and nonnegative,
matching the literature's positivity condition; Hermitian symmetry remains a separate
hypothesis as in Holevo's statement.

`IsConditionallyPositiveDefinite.schoenberg_exp` now applies to every additive group,
with assumptions only conditional positive definiteness and Hermitian symmetry, and
concludes `IsPositiveDefinite (fun x => exp (t * ψ x))` for all `t ≥ 0`. The earlier
normalization hypothesis `ψ 0 = 0` was unnecessary for Schoenberg's group theorem:
subtracting the constant `ψ 0` preserves conditional positive definiteness, Hermitian
symmetry makes `ψ 0` real, and the removed factor `exp(t ψ 0)` is a nonnegative real
scalar. The general closure theorem `IsPositiveDefinite.smul_nonneg` records the scalar
operation at the existing positive-definite function layer. The anchored-kernel
calculation and exponential-kernel argument remain private in `Schoenberg.lean`; the
matrix Schur step reuses `Matrix.PosSemidef.hadamard` instead of duplicating that result.
The real Lévy drift, Gaussian term, and compensated-integrand instances remain in
`LevyKhintchine/Representation.lean`, where their formulas belong.

The exact generic statements now appear in the module headers, while the
Lévy-specific exponent interface continues to use `ψ 0 = 0` because it must construct
probability measures from characteristic functions normalized to one at the identity.
The targets `Analysis.Fourier.PositiveDefinite`,
`Analysis.Fourier.ConditionallyPositiveDefinite.Schoenberg`, and
`Probability.Distributions.InfinitelyDivisible.LevyKhintchine.Representation` build
successfully with the pinned toolchain.

## Finite-product reindexing cover abstraction review (2026-10-21)

The previous `finiteCoordinateReindex` definition was a homogeneous `Fin n`
alias for `MeasurableEquiv.piCongrLeft`; its application lemma only exposed
the coordinate formula already provided by that Mathlib equivalence. Both
were removed, and the cyclic-corridor statements now refer directly to
`MeasurableEquiv.piCongrLeft`. This avoids a project wrapper that did not add
an operation beyond the pinned dependency API.

Mathlib revision
`380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51` provides
`measurePreserving_piCongrLeft` and `Measure.pi_map_piCongrLeft` for
reindexing dependent product measures, under coordinatewise sigma-finiteness
([pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Constructions/Pi.lean#L3194-L3224)).
The repository's `MeasureTheory.measure_le_card_smul_of_finite_cover_invariant`
already supplies the outer-measure inequality for any finite family of
measure-invariant preimages. These existing results cover the two lower-level
operations, so neither was duplicated or moved into a new public module.

The former `ProbabilityTheory.measure_pi_event_le_card_smul_of_reindex_cover`
assumed an identical probability measure in every coordinate. Mathlib's
`Measure.pi_map_piCongrLeft` accepts a sigma-finite family of coordinate
measures. The finite-cover estimate now assumes only that each coordinate
equivalence preserves that family, `ν (rotate k i) = ν i`, and concludes
`Measure.pi ν event ≤ Fintype.card κ • Measure.pi ν safe` whenever the
reindexed preimages of `safe` cover `event`. It now lives at
`MeasureTheory/Measure/Pi/FiniteReindexCover.lean`; the entrance argument
uses the identical-marginal IID instance.

The review checked the pinned
[`Constructions/Pi.lean`](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Constructions/Pi.lean#L745),
which states product-measure reindexing for coordinate families, and the
official Mathlib review guide's questions about existing general results,
semantic location, and the value of the proposed API
([review guide](https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/pr-review.html#location-location)).
The generic invariant-preimage cover inequality remains in
`MeasureTheory/OuterMeasure/Finite/Cover.lean`; the Pi-measure result provides
its coordinate-reindexing specialization without probability normalization.

## Finite-block oscillation and partition-range API review (2026-10-21)

This review used the current Mathlib API documentation and the repository's
pinned Mathlib source at revision
`380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51`. Mathlib's
[`oscillation`](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Analysis/Oscillation.html)
is the local topological oscillation of a function at a point, so it does not
represent the finite random-walk block event. Mathlib's
[`Metric.ediam`](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Topology/EMetricSpace/Diam.html)
does express a pairwise diameter bound for a set, but the block event is used
for arbitrary real widths, including negative widths; replacing its direct
pairwise predicate by a nonnegative extended diameter would add a side
condition and obscure the event's current meaning. The existing
`OscillationBounded` predicate already states the needed pairwise path bound,
so the finite-block event uses that representation.

The finite-block events now live in
`Probability/Process/RandomWalk/Path/Block/Oscillation.lean`; IID identities
between those events and partial-sum range probabilities live in
`Path/Block/Law/Oscillation.lean`; and the interval-partition product bounds
live in `Path/Block/Partition/Range.lean`. Their statements require only IID
increments and finite block data, so their former Mogulskii-specific location
was too narrow. The horizontal-tube module now applies the general
`iidSequenceLaw_measure_forall_consecutiveBlockEvent` directly instead of
exporting two event-specific wrappers. The normalized-step event bridge now
lives beside the variable-length normalized block path law in
`FunctionalLimit/NormalizedStep/Block.lean`.

Mathlib's pinned sources provide finite sums and measurable finite sums, but
no dedicated measurability theorem for `Fin.partialSum` on a finite increment
block. The new `Fin.measurable_partialSum` in
`MeasureTheory/Function/FinPartialSum.lean` states that missing interface for
any measurable additive monoid with measurable addition. It replaces the
duplicated recursive measurability proof in the independent-increments
finite-dimensional law and the private drawdown block-event helper, and it
serves the random-walk block-event proofs from the general measurable-function
layer. The Mathlib review used its pinned
`Fin.continuous_partialSum` result as the stronger topological counterpart.
This placement follows the repository's API rule and Mathlib's guidance to
look for an existing general result and choose the semantic owner before
adding declarations
([Mathlib review guide](https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/pr-review.html#location-location),
[Mathlib style guide](https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/style.html#header-and-imports)).

The range event and its probability had also been defined in
`Path/Corridor/Horizontal/Core.lean`, although neither depends on corridor
geometry. They now live in `Path/Event/Oscillation.lean`; the horizontal module
retains only the implication from tube confinement to range control and the
tube-specific probability results.

A citation scan of the Lean `Probability/` source tree found the thesis
references identify Wang Yiyang's *Asymptotic Speed of the N-Branching Random
Walk with Infinite Offspring* by author, title, institution, year, and cited
chapter/lemma or equation. Article references identify Aïdékon and Hu's
*Average-weight percolation on the complete graph* with its arXiv identifier
and proposition/equation. The scan found no generic `the paper` or `the thesis`
references and no private theorem names containing `paper` or `lemma33`; this
is a source-text check, while full citation normalization remains part of the
ongoing audit.

## Selection-mechanism abstraction review (2026-10-21)

The `Combinatorics.Selection.Mechanism` interface has the exact
interface `select : Set ι → Set ι` with `∀ s, select s ⊆ s`; its finite
counterpart has `select : Finset ι → Finset ι` with the analogous subset
property. The finite interface is used by `FiniteNSelection`, while the
set-valued interface is the base of `NSelection.toMechanism` and the random
selection APIs. The candidate for a more generic abstraction is a map
`f : α → α` on an arbitrary preorder with `∀ x, f x ≤ x`, instantiated at
`α = Set ι` with subset order.

The pinned Mathlib revision
`380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51` provides `OrderHom`, which also
requires monotonicity, and `ClosureOperator`, whose official API describes a
monotone, extensive, idempotent map. Using `ClosureOperator` on `OrderDual α`
encodes the corresponding anti-extensive, monotone, idempotent structure.
Those extra laws are absent from selection mechanisms and cannot be assumed: the
pointwise filter mechanism is a selection, while arbitrary mechanisms in the
interface are not required to preserve order or be idempotent. No bundled
arbitrary deflationary endomap API was found in the pinned `Mathlib/Order`
source. The existing domain-specific `Mechanism` therefore remains the
smallest faithful reusable interface; introducing a generic wrapper now would
add a second public type without another independently meaningful client.

The comparison used Mathlib's official
[closure-operator API documentation](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Order/Closure.html),
[library style guidance](https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/style.html),
and [contribution scope guidance](https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/index.html),
then checked `Mathlib/Order/Closure.lean` and the related order sources at the
pinned revision above. Mathlib's separate closure-operator structure shows
that bundled order operators encode their characteristic laws rather than
serving as arbitrary endomap wrappers. This review retains the current
selection abstraction and removes the one-use theorem that only packaged
`le_trans` in `Selection/Coupling/EndpointMinimum.lean`.

## Selection ownership review (2026-10-30)

The word *selection* names two different layers in this repository. In the
branching-selection literature, an N-branching random walk first branches and
then retains a prescribed number of particles at each generation; the
particle-system transition belongs under
`Combinatorics/BranchingWalk/Selection/`
([Bérard–Maillard](https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.1488)). The deterministic
`NSelection.Walk` and finite child-slot selection are kept in that layer.

By contrast, `Combinatorics.Selection.Mechanism` and
`Combinatorics.Selection.NSelection` have only an arbitrary candidate type,
sets or finite sets, cardinality, and order. They do not mention offspring,
generation, or genealogy. `MeasureTheory/Selection/` uses the same interface
to describe measurable and domain-flow selection rules, and
`Probability/Process/Stopping/Selection/Ranked.lean` specializes it to finite
ranked data at a stopping time. Those declarations are complete general
selection interfaces, so their deterministic base remains under
`Combinatorics/Selection/`; the branching-walk dynamics remain under
`Combinatorics/BranchingWalk/Selection/`.

The pinned Mathlib source provides generic finite-set filtering and sorting,
but no bundled `Set ι → Set ι` or `Finset ι → Finset ι` selection-mechanism
structure ([`Finset.filter`](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Data/Finset/Filter.html),
[`Finset.sort`](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Data/Finset/Sort.html)).
Mathlib's `Combinatorics/Compactness` also formalizes Rado's selection
principle as a combinatorial theorem; it is a compactness result rather than
an analogue of the repository's capacity-bounded selector interface
([module documentation](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Combinatorics/Compactness.html)).
The repository interface therefore remains a small deterministic base for
its measurable and process-level selection constructions.

## Parallel and concurrent process ownership review (2026-10-30)

The set-valued `parallelPopulation` and the concurrent-start construction
depend only on arbitrary index, state, and probability-space types. Their
adaptation statements use a `Filtration`; concurrent starts use Mathlib's
`IsStoppingTime`. Neither construction refers to branching, roots, offspring,
or genealogy, so their generic definitions and finite realizations now live
under `Probability/Process/Parallel/` and
`Probability/Process/Stopping/Concurrent/`. The root-indexed step-selection
and rooted-trial modules retain their adapters in
`Probability/BranchingRandomWalk/`. This ownership follows Mathlib's separate
process filtration and stopping-time APIs
([Filtration](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Probability/Process/Filtration.html),
[Stopping](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Probability/Process/Stopping.html)).

## Scalar-potential frontier abstraction review (2026-10-21)

The former `Cloud.lowerPotentialFrontier` and `Cloud.potentialValues` first
mapped particle positions through a real-valued potential and then projected
to `Cloud.support`. The deterministic `NSelection.Walk` frontier module
independently formed a `Finset` image of each generation, named it
`potentialPopulation`, and used its `min'` to define a scalar lower point.
That `Finset` wrapper and its membership theorem had no clients outside their
defining module. These two implementations share the geometric input
`CloudSet.points t` and the resulting sets
`φ '' C.points t` and its `IsLeast`/`IsGreatest` subsets.

The public abstraction now lives on `CloudSet`: for `C : CloudSet Time X` and
`φ : X → ℝ`, `CloudSet.potentialValues C φ t := φ '' C.points t`,
`CloudSet.lowerPotentialFrontier C φ t := (C.map φ).lowerFrontier t`, and
`CloudSet.upperPotentialFrontier C φ t := (C.map φ).upperFrontier t`. The lower
frontier has an explicit attainment predicate; when it holds,
`CloudSet.lowerPotentialPoint C φ t h` is a point of that frontier and is
least in `CloudSet.potentialValues C φ t`. This interface works for arbitrary
time-indexed clouds, including infinite slices. `Cloud` keeps its named
scalar-observation API as a specialization through `C.support`, which gives
clients with particle labels a direct interface. `Walk` now uses the
`CloudSet` API; its finite nonempty population proves attainment with
`Finset.exists_min_image`, and the redundant `potentialPopulation` API was
removed.

The research checked the official
[`Finset.min'` and `Finset.exists_min_image` APIs](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Data/Finset/Max.html)
and [`Set.exists_min_image`](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Data/Set/Finite/Lemmas.html),
then checked the repository's pinned Mathlib revision
`380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51`, including
`Mathlib/Order/Closure.lean` and `Mathlib/Data/Set/Finite/Lemmas.lean`.
Mathlib supplies generic extrema and images for finite sets, but no time-indexed
cloud potential-frontier semantics; using `Finset.min'` directly cannot serve
the arbitrary possibly infinite `Cloud` slices. The official closure-operator
documentation also explains why Mathlib retains a concrete closure interface
alongside a more general lower-adjoint interface: avoiding a ubiquitous
specialization parameter can justify a domain-specific convenience API. That
supports keeping the `Cloud` facade while placing the shared semantics on the
more general `CloudSet` layer.

## Asymptotic-speed and finite-selection abstraction review (2026-10-21)

The candidates were the normalized sequence predicate
`HasAsymptoticSpeed p c := Tendsto (fun n => (n : 𝕜)⁻¹ • p n) atTop (𝓝 c)` in
``Combinatorics/BranchingWalk/Selection/`NSelection/Walk/Speed.lean`, and the
finite threshold-count results in
``Combinatorics/BranchingWalk/Selection/`NSelection/Coupling/Finite.lean`:
`(retained.filter (fun p => position p ≤ a)).card ≤
((selectFirstN N rightCandidates).filter (fun q => candidatePosition q ≤ a)).card`,
under subset, capacity, threshold-count, and candidate-monotonicity hypotheses;
the second result derives a selected `q` with
`candidatePosition q ≤ position p` for each source `p` when `N > 0`.

The official Mathlib search and pinned source review found `Tendsto` as the
generic convergence interface, but no bundled asymptotic-speed predicate in
the pinned tree. `HasAsymptoticSpeed` has actual clients across the deterministic
N-selection and branching-random-walk limit modules, so it remains a named
semantic predicate at the deterministic trajectory layer; moving it under
`Probability/` would make its owner less general. Its public inventory now
records the normalized limit, uniqueness, fixed-index-shift equivalence,
frontier paths, and order-dual speed statement. Removed the unused reflexive
`hasAsymptoticSpeed_def`, the redundant one-step public wrapper
`hasAsymptoticSpeed_iff_succ` (its two clients now use the general shift theorem),
and the definitional `Walk.hasLowerFrontierSpeed_iff`. The coercion-only
order-dual equivalence remains private as a proof step.

Mathlib's official `Finset.sort` API constructs a sorted list and records its
length and sortedness; its finite extrema APIs provide `min'` and
`exists_min_image`. Those primitives do not state the threshold-count
comparison for a capped subpopulation against the first `N` candidates. The
repository's `Mechanism.ByValue.filter_card_le_filter_selectFirstNBy` handles
dynamic value-based selection; `Coupling/Finite` handles the distinct case
where a fixed identity order selects candidates and a monotonicity hypothesis
connects that order to observed positions. Both finite coupling statements are
consumed by `Cloud/Order/Selection.lean` and are useful independently of the
Cloud representation, so they remain public in `Selection/NSelection/Coupling/`
rather than moving into a theorem-specific `Lemmas/` directory.

The search used Mathlib's official
[`Finset.sort` documentation](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Data/Finset/Sort.html),
[`Finset` extrema documentation](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Data/Finset/Max.html),
and [Mathlib style guidance](https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/style.html),
then checked the pinned revision
`380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51` in
`Mathlib/`Data/Finset`/Sort.lean`, `Mathlib/`Data/Finset`/Max.lean`, and the
repository-wide search for an existing `HasAsymptoticSpeed` declaration.
`Speed.lean`, its probability client, `Coupling/Finite.lean`, and
`Cloud/Order/Selection.lean` build with the pinned toolchain.

## Multi-root selection-coupling API review (2026-10-21)

The public coupling family separates four mathematical stages. `Coupling/Cloud`
translates a finite spatial domination witness between population clouds into
`source.card ≤ target.card` and a canonical rank-matching injection;
`Coupling/Offspring` propagates a parent injection to the threshold-count
inequality for the child addresses
`(offspringAddresses sourceParents sourceSlots).filter (position ≤ a)`;
`Coupling/Step` constructs the one-generation injection into a first-`N`
population; `Coupling/Pathwise` iterates this pointwise in the sample and
generation indices. Their module docstrings now state the mathematical outputs
of each public entry.

The abstraction comparison checked Mathlib's `Finset.card_le_card_of_injOn`,
`Finset.card_filter_le`, `Finset.card_bij`, and `Finset.sort` in the official
documentation and pinned sources. These give the general finite counting,
injection, and ordering primitives, but they do not express the branching
object `offspringAddresses` or the implication from matched parent positions,
shared child slots, equal shared increments, and translation monotonicity to
lower-tail child-count domination. `Coupling/Offspring` records that complete
finite branching result for arbitrary root-indexed walks and arbitrary child
slot sets, so its two theorems remain a named reusable coupling interface;
they are not merely calls to Mathlib's raw cardinality facts. The supporting
stages also remain in their semantic `Cloud/`, `Offspring.lean`, `Step.lean`,
and `Pathwise.lean` modules rather than being presented as one flat list of
unrelated helper files. The `Coupling/` directory has five direct Lean modules,
below the repository's eight-file grouping review threshold.

The comparison used Mathlib's official
[`Finset` cardinality documentation](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Data/Finset/Card.html)
and [`Finset.sort` documentation](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Data/Finset/Sort.html),
then checked `Mathlib/`Data/Finset`/Card.lean` and
`Mathlib/`Data/Finset`/Sort.lean` at pinned revision
`380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51`.

## Branching ancestry and list-prefix abstraction review (2026-10-21)

`IsDescendant β p q` is the relation
`∃ t, q = (p.1, p.2 ++ t) ∧ surviveAlong (β.step p.1) p.2 t`. The candidate
general abstraction is the list-prefix relation on addresses. Lean's
`List.IsPrefix` captures `p.2 <+: q.2`, and Mathlib's descriptive-set-theory
tree formalization treats a tree as a set of finite sequences closed under
prefixes. Those structures represent address shape; they do not encode the
walk-dependent survival condition along the ancestor's root-indexed step
field. `IsDescendant` therefore remains owned by `BranchingWalk/Basic/Genealogy`
and retains the suffix witness that simultaneously records the prefix and its

`Descendant`, and `GenerationSize`, so no helper-only subgroup is needed.

## Path displacement and generic list folds (2026-10-21)

`displace β v p` is defined by
`displace β v [] = 0` and
`displace β v (i :: p) = value' (β v) i + displace β (v ++ [i]) p`.
The candidate abstraction is `List.foldl` with an accumulator carrying both
the current address and accumulated displacement. Mathlib's generic
`List.foldl_append` states the composition law for such a fold; the module's
`displace_append` is its domain-specific form,
`displace β v (p ++ q) = displace β v p + displace β (v ++ p) q`.
The fold accumulator must still update the address using the traversed path and
read each mark from the corresponding `StepField`; spelling that stateful fold
out would add a second representation without another client. The recursive
definition plus `displace_append` and the finite-sum bridge lemmas therefore
remain the public displacement interface in `Basic/Position/Displace.lean`.
The missing `displace_nil` formula was added to that module's declaration list.
`Basic/Position/` has three direct modules, all describing the displacement
object, its path operations, or maps of the field.

The abstraction check used the official
[`List.foldl_append` documentation](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Init/Data/List/Lemmas.html)
and [Mathlib's list-fold API](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Data/List/Basic.html),
then checked `Mathlib/Data/List/Basic.lean` at pinned revision
`380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51`.

## Ulam--Harris tree representations and directory ownership (2026-10-21)

The candidate generic representation is Mathlib's
[`Descriptive.tree α`](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/SetTheory/Descriptive/Tree.html),
a complete sublattice of sets of finite lists closed under prefixes. The
repository's `UlamHarris.Tree α` also requires `[] ∈ T.carrier` and
`u ++ [j] ∈ T.carrier ∧ i < j → u ++ [i] ∈ T.carrier`. Those root and ordered
sibling conditions encode the canonical Ulam--Harris offspring labels. Thus
`Descriptive.tree` supplies the generic prefix-closed-tree layer, but replacing
the local type with it would erase defining branching semantics. The local
parent-closure axiom is equivalent to prefix closure; no change to the
established `Tree` representation is needed for that equivalence.

Mathlib's descriptive-tree API provides reusable prefix operations such as
`Tree.take`, `Tree.subAt`, and `Tree.pullSub`. The production Ulam--Harris
modules currently have no clients for these operations. An isolated conversion
wrapper would therefore add an API without an active reuse site; introduce that
bridge if a generic prefix-tree operation is needed by a concrete client.
Where generic graph semantics are already used, the existing `Tree/Graph/`
family is substantive: it defines parent--child `Digraph` and `Quiver`
projections and an undirected `SimpleGraph`, then exposes arborescence,
connectedness, acyclicity, and tree-isomorphism results. These are complete
cross-representation interfaces, so they remain outside `Lemmas/`.

The directory now distinguishes four mathematical meanings. `Tree/Finite/`
contains the finite-carrier predicate and its topological subtype;
`Tree/Truncation/` contains the operation retaining addresses through depth
`n` and the agreement-height invariant used by the tree metric;
`Tree/Topology/FiniteLabels.lean` contains the finite-label Borel equality;
and `Tree/Graph/` contains the graph representations. This moves generic
finite-depth operations out of the finite-carrier directory and the finite
label topology theorem beside its topology subject. Each moved source header
now lists its public statements; the graph files remain grouped by the
properties they establish.

This comparison used the official Mathlib documentation for
[`Descriptive.tree`](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/SetTheory/Descriptive/Tree.html),
[`Quiver.Arborescence`](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Combinatorics/Quiver/Arborescence.html),
and [`SimpleGraph.IsTree`](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Acyclic.html),
then checked the vendored Mathlib source at pinned revision
`380f2aafb622cb2c1c93dac545b6389083c68c51`.

`RootIndexed.Tree.treeDist_bddAbove` was made private: it only supplies a

## Conditioned transition proof modules and Portmanteau abstraction (2026-10-21)

`Transition/Event.lean` defines the finite corridor event
\(D_{n,\Delta}=\{0\le S_j\le 5\Delta/6\ (1\le j\le n),\;
S_n\in[5\Delta/12,11\Delta/24]\}\), its normalized path realization,
and its diffusive horizon. `Factorization.lean` provides the finite-block
measurability and IID prefix/suffix product interfaces used by multiple
small-deviation clients. `DiffusiveLower.lean` contains the final public
\(C\Delta^{-2}\) transition estimate used by the entrance argument. These
three modules remain at the `Transition/` subject level.

The other five modules (`Meander/CorridorProbability`,
`Meander/FromFirstWindow`, `Meander/FromMeander`,
`Diffusive/ConditionalProbability`, and `Diffusive/SurvivalLower`) form intermediate
steps of the single Appendix A.2, Lemma A.7 proof chain. Their current clients
are confined to that chain, so they now live under the one
`Transition/Lemmas/` subtree, split into `Meander/` and `Diffusive/`. The
interfaces they use at broader levels remain with their mathematical owners:
open-set probability transfer is in `Probability/ConvergenceInDistribution/Portmanteau.lean`,
the IID cyclic-rotation inequality is in
`RandomWalk/Fluctuation/SparreAndersen/Rotation/Probability.lean`, and the
finite-variance endpoint-sign limit is in
`RandomWalk/Fluctuation/FiniteVarianceSignLimit.lean`. Thus the transition
subtree keeps the theorem-specific probability estimates while general
Portmanteau, rotation, and sign-limit statements remain reusable outside it.

The abstraction review checked Mathlib's official
[`MeasureTheory.Measure.Portmanteau` API](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Measure/Portmanteau.html):
`ProbabilityMeasure.le_liminf_measure_open_of_tendsto` already proves
\(\mu(G)\le\liminf_n\mu_n(G)\) for open \(G\), and the local
`TendstoInDistribution.exists_eventually_measure_map_ge_pos_of_isOpen`
specializes this to a uniform positive lower bound when the limiting open-set
mass is positive. The support-to-positive-mass step already uses Mathlib's
`Measure.mem_support_iff_forall`. No additional corridor-specific generic
wrapper is needed.

The reference audit found that Caravenna--Chaumont equation (3.3) is the
weak-convergence statement for the rescaled meander, while equation (1.7)
defines the path rescaling map. The event/path equivalence now cites (1.7);
the elementary conditional-probability factorization cites Wang Yiyang,
*Asymptotic Speed of the N-Branching Random Walk with Infinite Offspring*,
Appendix A.2, Lemma A.7, without attributing that identity to equation (3.3).
The PDF was checked at the authors' hosted copy of
[*Invariance principles for random walks conditioned to stay positive*](https://chaumont.pages.math.cnrs.fr/rpdfiles/carcha.pdf).

## IID stopping-time block API review (2026-10-22)

The stopping-time block results in
`Probability/Sequence/IID/Blocks/StoppingTime.lean` were checked against the
pinned Mathlib stopping-time and independence interfaces. Mathlib provides
`IsStoppingTime` for discrete filtrations and general independence results
for finite families and processes, including `iIndepFun.indepFun_finset`; the
reviewed APIs do not provide the factorization of a finite future block on a
stopping-time cell. The local cell theorem supplies that missing combination
for a canonical IID sequence and an arbitrary measurable finite-block event.
Its bounded-stopping-time theorem sums the cell identities, and its
unbounded-event inequality follows by summing the disjoint finite cells.

These are complete IID-sequence probability statements used by the
random-walk first-crossing interfaces, rather than derivations belonging to
one small-deviation proof. They therefore remain in the public
`Probability/Sequence/IID/Blocks/` family. No additional abstract
independent-but-not-identically-distributed stopping-time interface was
introduced: the inspected repository has no client for it, and Mathlib's
finite-set independence API already supplies the lower-level mechanism.
This decision follows the abstraction criterion that a new public API should
state a reusable mathematical interface, not merely package a proof pattern.

The source comparison used Mathlib's official documentation for
[`Probability.Process.Stopping`](https://leanprover-community.github.io/mathlib4_docs/Mathlib/Probability/Process/Stopping.html),
